AAI.name: Asian Alliance International Public Company Limited
AAI.thesis: Debt-free OEM pet-food exporter with a sharply weaker Q1 2026 — revenue -17.1% YoY and GPM 7.3pp below year-ago as US/Canada customers cut orders on tariff risk — while the upstream loan to parent ASIAN has triggered an RPT size test ahead of the 1 Jul 2026 rule change; balance sheet strength keeps this Watch rather than worse.
AAI.summary: Q1 2026 (Q1/69) revenue fell 17.1% YoY to THB 1,558mn and gross profit halved (-49.7% YoY) as US/Canada pet-food customers — still ~47% of revenue after dropping from ~57% — adjusted orders to manage tariff risk, compounded by USD depreciation and lost fixed-cost absorption. GPM of 11.2% sits below the company's own 13-16% FY target, yet management held FY2026 guidance of THB 7,600mn (+8% YoY), which now requires a strong recovery: Q1 delivered only 20.5% of the revenue target. The financial position is the offset: zero bank debt, net cash, current ratio 6.0x, OCF of THB 491mn comfortably above net profit, and the THB 800mn capex program (automated warehouse live early Q3/69, Building 3) self-funded. Governance is the live issue — the upstream loan to 70% parent ASIAN (THB 412.4mn outstanding, THB 932.8mn gross flow in Q1 alone at 3.33-3.55%) exceeds the preliminary 3%-of-NTA size test ~2.8x, and an unnamed related party supplied THB 39.7mn of raw materials (+252.6% YoY). JARVIS follow-ups are due 15 Jun 2026.
AAI.business: OEM manufacturer (94.7% of pet-food revenue) and distributor of pet food, shelf-stable human food, and tuna by-products; subsidiary of Asian Sea Corporation (ASIAN, 70%). Exports dominate: US/Canada ~47%, Europe ~31%, Middle East ~8% of Q1/69 revenue.
financialSnapshot: Q1/69: revenue THB 1,558mn (-17.1% YoY, -11.6% QoQ), gross profit THB 175mn (-49.7% YoY), GPM 11.2% (-7.3pp YoY), net profit THB 137mn (-46.9% YoY but +25.3% QoQ), NPM 8.8% (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.1, s.3).
Volume: total -7.8% YoY to 11,514 tons; OEM pet food -12.8% while own-brand pet food +37.8% on domestic affordable-segment push (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.2.1-2.2).
Balance sheet: zero bank borrowings, D/E 0.2x, net cash position, current ratio 6.0x, cash THB 813mn (+453% YTD) (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.8, s.11).
Cash: OCF THB 491mn (+23.7% YoY) vs net profit THB 137mn; AR days improved to 44 from 54; ASIAN loan repayment returned THB 295mn (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.7).
Market: THB 3.48, -15.5% YTD, PE 11.9x, PBV 1.49x, DY 9.6% (dashboard ticker-summary).
mdaSynthesis: The quarter's miss is volume-led: US/Canada customers adjusted orders to manage tariff-related risk; management notes reciprocal-tariff reductions in early 2026 should support competitiveness ahead, but gives no rate detail or mitigation plan (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.2.3, s.12).
Geographic rebalancing underway: US/Canada share fell ~57% to ~47% while Europe rose to ~31% and domestic to ~10% — partially absorbing the North America decline (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.2.3).

Management reaffirmed FY2026 targets at the 28 May Opportunity Day: revenue THB 7,600mn (+8% YoY; pet food 6,800mn, human food 800mn), GPM 13-16%, capex THB 800mn self-funded (OPPDAY-AAI-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md).

Efficiency capex on track: second automated warehouse (>15,000 pallets) in system testing, operations from early Q3/69; 116 new SKUs launched under the LEVEL UP AAI strategy (OPPDAY-AAI-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md).
No buyback program despite the cash pile — management said one would need board approval and is only under consideration (OPPDAY-AAI-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md Q&A).
fsNotesSynthesis: Upstream loan to parent ASIAN: outstanding THB 412.4mn at 31 Mar 2026 (down from 707.2mn), but Q1 gross flow was THB 932.8mn (319.0mn new + 613.8mn repaid) at 3.33-3.55% p.a. (NOTES_AAI_2026Q1_T.md Note 2).

Raw-material purchases from an unnamed related party (common shareholders/directors, not ASIAN): THB 39.7mn in Q1/69 vs 11.3mn Q1/68 (+252.6% YoY), cost-plus pricing, no MD&A explanation (NOTES_AAI_2026Q1_T.md Note 2).
Customer concentration: top-2 customers = 44.2% of revenue per FS Note 6; the MD&A never names them (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.2.4, s.12).
Other income THB 40mn (+55.4% YoY) includes Vayupak dividend THB 13mn and unrealized FX gain THB 23mn — low quality, excluded from cash flow (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.3.2).
Effective tax rate 10.7% on continuing BOI privileges (MDA_AAI_2026Q1_T.md s.10).

Revenue -17.1% YoY is genuine demand/order-timing weakness in US/Canada OEM (no non-recurring revenue items), with top-2 customers at 44.2% of revenue. Brand growth (+37.8% volume) is the right direction but only ~3.6% of pet-food revenue.

sixThemes.outlook: Guidance held but back-loaded: THB 7,600mn FY target implies ~+8% YoY while Q1 ran -17.1%; Q1 is only 20.5% of target. Recovery thesis rests on tariff easing, US customer re-ordering, and Q3 warehouse efficiencies — none yet evidenced in numbers.

AIMCG.name: AIM COMMERCIAL GROWTH FREEHOLD AND LEASEHOLD REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST
AIMCG.thesis: Shrinking commercial REIT in wind-down dynamics: 72 Courtyard divested, expected-credit-loss charges of THB 35mn against THB 65mn of quarterly income, distributions now paid as capital reduction rather than income, and the unit at 0.17x book — the surveillance posture is asset-runoff monitoring, not growth coverage.
AIMCG.summary: Q1/2026 total investment income was THB 65.3mn (-1.8% YoY), still reflecting the Q4/2025 divestment of the 72 Courtyard project. The dominant item is credit quality: an expected-credit-loss allowance on rental and service receivables of THB 35.0mn was recorded this quarter — more than half of quarterly income — driving an expense line up 130.7% YoY. Net assets from operations were barely positive at THB 1.5mn (vs -5.3mn a year ago), and no asset revaluation was recognized. The structural signal is the May-June 2026 sequence of capital-reduction disclosures (HIGH severity, 11 May and 10-11 Jun): AIMCG is returning capital to unitholders in lieu of income distributions, consistent with a portfolio (UD Town, Porto Chino, Noble Solo condo units, post-72 Courtyard) that no longer generates distributable income at the prior scale. At THB 1.33 (-24.4% YTD) the unit trades at 0.17x book. The RM task here is runoff surveillance: tenant credit (who is behind the THB 35mn ECL), remaining asset values, and whether the trust has a path back to income distributions or continues shrinking.
AIMCG.business: Commercial/retail-mixed REIT holding leasehold/sublease rights in UD Town (Udon Thani) and Porto Chino (Mahachai), plus commercial condominium ownership in Noble Solo (Thonglor); 72 Courtyard was divested in Q4/2025. REIT Manager: AIM Real Estate Management.

ALLY.summary: Q1/2026 total revenue was THB 382.6mn, up 0.3% YoY though down 8.8% QoQ off the Q4 high season. At THB 4.70 (+7.8% YTD, one of few Champ PF&REIT names up this year), trailing yield 9.43% and 0.47x book, the market treats ALLY as a stable yield vehicle with limited growth. Watch items are the standard retail-REIT set: tenant renewals across 15 community malls, leasehold amortization drag on NAV, and what the manager does next with the capacity freed by the Sai Mai cancellation. Vault depth is moderate (no health check yet; MD&A + FS notes + NotebookLM snapshot available).

AMATA.name: AMATA CORPORATION PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
AMATA.thesis: Industrial-estate developer printing a record quarter — net profit +66% YoY on a 57% land-sale GPM mix shift toward Amata City Chonburi — but Q1 presales of just 106 rai against a 2,800-rai FY target, ODI-stalled Vietnam transfers, and an unresolved Large-RPT intragroup loan stack keep this Watch despite the beat.
AMATA.summary: Q1/69 revenue rose 17.9% YoY to THB 3,996mn and attributable net profit jumped 66.3% to THB 1,379mn, beating consensus by ~45-53%. The driver is mix: land-sale revenue +30% YoY to THB 2,486mn with 88% from higher-margin Amata City Chonburi, lifting land GPM to 57% (from 55%) and blended GPM to a five-quarter-high 44.2%. The forward indicators are the concern: Q1 presales were only 106 rai versus 306-307 rai transferred (drawing down the THB 19,704mn backlog), Vietnam transferred just 0.1 rai on Chinese-customer ODI approval delays (~240 rai pending per management), and associate profit fell ~34% YoY on Amata B.Grimm FX and Amata NGD derivative losses. Governance moved: Vikrom Kromadit (26.23% holder) shifted from Chairman to CEO on 14 May 2026, with Dr. Panpree Bahiddha-Nukara as Chairman. The JARVIS health check recalculated NTA to THB 21,224mn, dropping the 3% Large-RPT threshold to THB 637mn — the THB 1,060mn long-term intragroup loans (4.99% of NTA) classify as Large RPT, and the 73%-held AMATAV gets no >=90% exemption under ทจ. 46/2568 from 1 Jul 2026. D/E covenant headroom is adequate but not wide (1.7x vs 1.5-2.75x caps), Vietnam subsidiaries operate on a covenant waiver, and no bonds mature within 12 months (A-/TRIS).
AMATA.business: Develops and manages industrial estates in Thailand (Amata City Chonburi/Rayong), Vietnam (AMATAV, group 73%), and Laos (Natuey, Namor — pre-revenue), plus utilities (power, water, gas) and ready-built factory rentals. FY69 land-sales target 2,800 rai (Thailand 1,650 / Vietnam 550 / Laos 600).

AP.name: AP (THAILAND) PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
AP.thesis: Market leader in Bangkok low-rise with a deep 39,626mn backlog covering near-term revenue, but a 11,500mn bond wall (41% of outstanding) due within 12 months, GPM compression of 160–290bps YoY, and a 12-JV RPT structure with Mitsubishi Estate (51/49) that has not been cleared under ทจ. 46/2568 ahead of the 1 Jul 2026 effective date — three concurrently open risks keep this Watch.
AP.summary: AP reported Q1/2026 consolidated revenue of THB 9,547mn (+24.0% YoY, IFRS basis) and net profit of THB 903mn (+4.6% YoY), with EPS of THB 0.29. Revenue growth was driven by condo transfer commencement (ASPIRE Itsaraphap, GOOD DAY Sukhumvit 93) and low-rise expansions. However quality is mixed: consolidated GPM contracted to 29.6% (property-only 28.1%) from ~31–32% in Q1/2025, a compression of 160–290bps attributed to price promotions and construction cost inflation. Presales of THB 11,215mn declined 7.4% YoY reflecting market softening, though the 30 Apr 2026 backlog stood at THB 39,626mn (low-rise 18,476 + condo 21,150), providing solid forward visibility. Net D/E of 0.64x is the lowest among the peer group. The critical risk is the bond wall: 17 tranches totalling THB 28,000mn outstanding, with THB 11,500mn (41%) due within 12 months including the CRITICAL AP267A+B (THB 2,000mn) maturing July 2026. Additionally, AP's 12 active 51/49 JVs with Mitsubishi Estate create an unresolved RPT compliance exposure under ทจ. 46/2568 — AP controls each JV at 51%, meaning all land sales, management fees, and development services to JVs are RPTs without the ≥90% exemption. The aggregate size of these flows may exceed the THB 1,409mn Large RPT threshold. A new Audit Committee member was appointed 14 May 2026 — independence verification pending.
AP.business: Residential property developer focused on Bangkok and surrounds, operating ~212 active projects across low-rise brands (Pleno, Centro, The City, The Palazzo, Baan Klang Muang, Grande Pleno, APITOWN for upcountry) and condo brands (Aspire, Life, The Address, Good Day, Rhythm). Operates 12 active 51/49 JV projects with Mitsubishi Estate Asia/MJR (Premium Residence JV umbrella, registered capital THB 12,619mn); cumulative JV project value ~THB 137,000mn across 31 projects. FY2026 Q2 launch pipeline of 12 projects totalling THB 17,150mn including LIFE Sukhumvit–Rama 4 (JV flagship).
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 9,547mn (+24.0% YoY IFRS; management basis 10,554mn), net profit THB 903mn (+4.6%), NPM 9.5%, EPS THB 0.29 — earnings growth lagged revenue due to GPM compression (NOTES_AP_2026Q1_T.md Note 3; HC AP.md Theme 3).

GPM consolidated 29.6%; property-only 28.1% — down ~160–290bps YoY from ~31–32% driven by price promotions and construction cost inflation; Krungsri revised FY2026 NP forecast down 8% to THB 4,500mn (MDA_AP_2026Q1_T.md Section 1).

Presales Q1/2026: THB 11,215mn (-7.4% YoY), split low-rise 8,761mn / condo 2,453mn; backlog at 30 Apr 2026: THB 39,626mn (low-rise 18,476 + condo 21,150mn from 5 projects targeting FY2026 transfer) (MDA_AP_2026Q1_T.md Sections 2–3).

Balance sheet: total assets THB 87,646mn, equity 46,981mn, IBD inferred ~32,577mn, net D/E 0.64x — lowest among PROP peer group; ThaiBMA bond outstanding THB 28,000mn across 17 tranches (AP.md auto-thaibma-bonds; HC Theme 6).
OCF Q1/2025 was (939mn); Q1/2026 OCF not yet directly extracted — expected negative by developer seasonality (HC AP.md Theme 4 PENDING flag).
mdaSynthesis: Management highlighted 6 sold-out projects in Q1/2026 worth THB 6,175mn as evidence of genuine demand, and stressed Net D/E 0.64x discipline; also announced upcountry expansion via APITOWN brand (Saraburi, Hua Hin) — first forays outside Bangkok (MDA_AP_2026Q1_T.md Section 6).

The latest JV project APME27 was established Q1/2026 and 49% sold to MEA/MJR for THB 0.5mn (stub price) on 14 May 2026 per SET ID 104284100 — standard JV formation pattern, MT analysis indicates Small MT pending NA-APME27 confirmation (AP-RPT-2026-05-18.md Section 4).

Q2/2026 launch pipeline: 12 projects, THB 17,150mn including semi-detached, SDH, LIFE Sukhumvit–Rama 4 JV (4,500mn), and two APITOWN upcountry projects (1,600mn) — management presented this as demand-justified momentum (MDA_AP_2026Q1_T.md Section 4).

GPM compression not fully explained in the secondary-sourced MD&A extract; root cause split between promotion discounts, construction cost inflation, and mix from newly-launched low-margin projects (Rangsit, 250mn revenue only in Q1) remains open — primary PDF still needs review (NOTES_AP_2026Q1_T.md Warning).

Revenue reconciliation: a second presales figure of THB 20,645mn appearing in media likely represents YTD or 1H preliminary — not the Q1 standalone; needs confirmation from primary MD&A (NOTES_AP_2026Q1_T.md Note 4).
fsNotesSynthesis: JV structure: AP holds 51% in each JV (12 active), partner Mitsubishi Estate Asia + MJR hold 49% collectively; AP controls each JV → JVs are Related Persons under ทจ. 46/2568; AP's 51% holding falls below the ≥90% intragroup exemption threshold — RPT applies to all land sales, management fees, and development services flowing AP→JV (NOTES_AP_2026Q1_T.md Note 6; AP-RPT-2026-05-18.md Section 2).

NA proxy for Large RPT threshold: equity 46,981mn → 3% = THB 1,409mn; aggregate value of land sales + management fees + dev services to 12 JVs over the 6-month aggregation window is not yet extracted from primary FS Notes — if it exceeds 1,409mn this is a Large RPT requiring IFA + SH vote before 1 Jul 2026 (AP-RPT-2026-05-18.md Section 3).

Bond wall: 17 tranches outstanding (ThaiBMA 12 May 2026): AP267B (1,500mn, Jul 2026) + AP267A (500mn, Jul 2026) = 2,000mn CRITICAL within 2 months; AP26925A/29A/29B = 4,500mn by Sep 2026; AP26DA + AP271A = 5,000mn by Jan 2027; total ≤12 months = 11,500mn (41% of total) (AP.md auto-thaibma-bonds; HC AP.md Theme 6).

sixThemes.salesQuality: LOW-MED. Backlog THB 39,626mn as of 30 Apr 2026 provides strong Q2–Q4 revenue visibility — 5 condo projects totalling 21,150mn target FY2026 transfer. sixThemes.costMargin: MED. GPM declining for the third consecutive year — property GPM 28.1% is ~290bps below Q1/2025 and ~600bps below FY2023 peaks. sixThemes.workingCapital: PENDING. OCF Q1/2026 not extracted — this is a critical gap. Q1/2025 was (939mn); given 24% revenue growth the working capital build could be larger in absolute terms. sixThemes.cashFunding: MED-HIGH. Net D/E 0.64x is conservatively positioned relative to peers, but the bond wall of THB 11,500mn due within 12 months — notably AP267A+B (2,000mn) maturing Jul 2026 just 6–7 weeks away — is the primary funding risk. AP has a demonstrated track record of rolling bonds, but market conditions may push refinancing costs higher. Covenant terms unconfirmed (HC AP.md Theme 6; AP.md auto-thaibma-bonds).
sixThemes.outlook: MED. FY2026 backlog coverage is strong; Q2 launch pipeline of 17,150mn is active. Key risks are GPM recovery trajectory (presales still declining YoY, which will pressure future margins), bond wall execution in H2/2026, and JV RPT framework compliance. If the July bond is rolled successfully and the JV RPT is resolved, tone upgrade to Neutral is supportable.

AQUA.name: AQUA CORPORATION PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
AQUA.thesis: Deep-restructuring holding company whose pivot into restaurants produced its first profitable quarter (THB 39.4mn vs a 92.4mn loss) on revenue up 351% YoY — but the gross margin collapsed from 61% to 25% on the mix change, the current ratio sits at 0.65x, and two straight years of ~THB 1bn losses mean one good quarter does not clear the Watch.
AQUA.summary: Q1/2026 marks AQUA's swing to profit: total revenue THB 417.7mn (+351% YoY from 92.6mn) with the restaurant business contributing THB 330.6mn (79% of revenue), net profit THB 39.4mn versus a THB 92.4mn loss in Q1/2025, and EBITDA THB 96.4mn versus 32.5mn. The share of JV results also flipped positive (THB +59.4mn vs -48.2mn). Quality caveats are heavy: gross margin fell from 60.7% to 24.8% because the acquired restaurant/healthcare operations carry a structurally higher cost base than the legacy portfolio; the current ratio is 0.65x (quick ratio weaker), the lowest liquidity in Champ's FOOD coverage; and the FY2025 base was a THB 1,082mn net loss (NPM -112%) after impairments, following a THB 988mn loss in FY2024. The stock trades at THB 0.10 (PBV 0.14x, -33% YTD) — the market is pricing residual distress. Vault coverage is thin (no health check, no earnings call, no RPT triage), so this report leans on the auto-ingested MD&A and FS-notes; a full 6-Theme health check is the next step if the RM book keeps AQUA active.
AQUA.business: Investment holding company in transition: legacy media/billboard and rental assets being replaced by restaurant operations (79% of Q1/2026 revenue) and a healthcare/medical-specialist business; JV exposures remain on the balance sheet.

ASIAN.name: ASIAN SEA CORPORATION PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
ASIAN.thesis: ASIAN's Q1/2026 headline profit of THB 125.5mn masks a structural GPM collapse to 10.7% (from 15.9% a year ago) driven by US-tariff-induced pet food order deferral and a low-margin squid mix surge, while an unresolved upstream RPT — the parent borrowing THB 412mn from its 70%-owned subsidiary AAI at sub-market rates — is the governance priority under ทจ. 46/2568.
ASIAN.summary: ASIAN reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 2,408mn (−10.5% YoY, −18.2% QoQ), net profit THB 125.5mn (−38.2% YoY), and GPM collapsing to 10.7% from 15.9% in Q1/2025. The primary culprit is product-mix: canned pet food (lower margin) now represents ~50% of pet food sales, and squid has expanded to ~48% of frozen seafood revenue — both driven by US customer logistics/tariff management behavior rather than structural demand loss. Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue growth guidance of +10.8% and GPM target of 13–15%, contingent on pet food US tariff stabilization and recovery in higher-margin VAP orders. The balance sheet is pristine at the ASIAN standalone level — D/E 0.19x, cash THB 818mn (per Q1 oppday), zero bank borrowings. The red-flag item is governance: ASIAN itself is the borrower from subsidiary AAI (THB 412.4mn outstanding at Q1/69, 3.33–3.55% p.a.) — an upstream RPT that has triggered a Size Test against ASIAN's NTA and attracted an IFA opinion from the AAI side (19 Mar 2026). The Q1 auditor conclusion is clean (TSRE 2410). Aqua Feed (+11.3% YoY) and Shelf Stable Food (+31.7% QoQ) are bright spots; the re-engagement of US pet food customers is the key H2 re-rating catalyst.
ASIAN.business: Holding company producing and exporting processed frozen seafood, pet food (OEM/ODM via 70%-subsidiary AAI), aquaculture feed, and shelf-stable tuna products. Four segments: Pet Food & Fish Meal (~56% of Q1/2026 revenue), Frozen Seafood (~27%), Shelf Stable Food (~9%), and Aqua Feed (~8%). US and ASEAN are primary export markets. ASIAN guarantees THB 568mn of AAI's bank credit facilities (standalone contingent liability).

GPM 10.7% vs 15.9% in Q1/2025 — margin compression from unfavorable mix: canned pet food ~50% of pet food, squid ~48% of frozen seafood (OPPDAY-ASIAN-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md).

mdaSynthesis: Revenue decline was driven by US-customer order deferral in pet food — major US buyers managed tariff uncertainty and logistics timing, causing a −10.5% YoY drop in the Pet Food & Fish Meal segment (to THB 1,360mn); management expects improved cadence from Q2 onward (MDA_ASIAN_2026Q1_E.md; OPPDAY-ASIAN-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md).

Mix shift the GPM driver, not price collapse: canned pet food proportion expanded to ~50% of pet food sales (lower margin than pouch/kibble); squid expanded to ~48% of frozen seafood (low-margin commodity) — both are tactical order responses, not structural (OPPDAY-ASIAN-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md).

Aqua Feed bright spot: THB 187mn (+11.3% YoY) — management is investing in lab R&D and trial farms to compete on feed-conversion ratios; competitor volumes grew faster (+16% YoY) but ASIAN's Q1/2026 exceeded Q1/2025 as early sign of stabilization (OPPDAY-ASIAN-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md Q&A).

FY2026 targets reaffirmed: Pet Food & Fish Meal THB 6,800mn, Frozen Seafood THB 3,120mn, Aqua Feed THB 1,015mn, Shelf Stable Food THB 800mn — total ~THB 11,735mn (+10.8%); GPM target 13–15% (OPPDAY-ASIAN-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md forward guidance).

Real estate JV temporarily suspended for business plan review — management cited market volatility and revised assumptions; no financial impact disclosed but confirms capex prioritization (OPPDAY-ASIAN-2026-05-28-2026Q1.md strategic initiatives).
fsNotesSynthesis: RPT note confirms: ASIAN (via group subsidiaries) had intragroup purchases of raw materials from related parties of THB 1,061 thousand (Q1/2026) vs THB 1,271 thousand (Q1/2025) — separate small item. The material RPT is the upstream loan: AAI's FS notes confirm THB 412,400 thousand outstanding from ASIAN at 3.33–3.55% p.a. as at 31 Mar 2026 (NOTES_ASIAN_2026Q1_E.md; AAI-RPT-2026-05-17.md).

ASIAN standalone has no bank IBD — FS notes confirm only lease liabilities and subsidiary-level group obligations; the THB 568mn guarantee to AAI bank facilities remains the key contingent liability (2-Analysis/AI-Generated/02-Health Check Log/2026_Q1/ASIAN.md Theme 1).

Two major customers (>10% of revenue each) in Q1/2026 contributed THB 689mn from the feedstuff/pet food segment — down from three major customers in Q1/2025; concentration risk in pet food remains high (NOTES_ASIAN_2026Q1_E.md Segment/Revenue Evidence).

No new financial standards impacting the FS in 2026 (NOTES_ASIAN_2026Q1_E.md basis of preparation); auditor CPA No. 6140 issued a clean TSRE 2410 review conclusion dated 5 May 2026 (AUDITOR_ASIAN_2026Q1_E.md).

AWC.name: ASSET WORLD CORP PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
AWC.thesis: AWC's Q1/2026 record net profit of THB 1,986mn is 76.6% driven by a non-recurring fair-value property revaluation gain of THB 1,522mn; normalized EBITDA growth of +3.3% YoY confirms the underlying hotel (+12% rev) and commercial (+16% rev) engines are sound, but the TCC Group RPT ecosystem complexity — intercompany standalone loans of ~THB 71.8bn, two ROFO/ROFR non-exercises in four months, and a deleted CG Policy section in the latest 56-1 — demands urgent pre-assessment before ทจ.46/2568 takes effect 1 July 2026.
AWC.summary: AWC reported Q1/2026 consolidated revenue of THB 6,776mn (+9.5% YoY per oppday), EBITDA THB 3,531mn (+3.3% YoY), and net profit THB 1,986mn (+1% YoY). The profit headline is materially inflated by a THB 1,522mn investment-property FV gain; excluding this, normalized core profit is approximately THB 464mn. Hotel segment delivered RevPAR of THB 5,230/night, EA Rooftop achieved a new quarterly record at THB 158mn. The commercial segment grew +16% YoY with Retail EBITDA +35% YoY. Balance sheet metrics: IBD/E 0.87x, avg cost of debt 2.54% (guided to fall to 2.50% in May), avg maturity 3.2 years. The company targets 35 hotels / 9,312 keys by 2030 (from current base). On governance, the CG Policy section was deleted from 56-1 Y68 (similarity 0% vs prior year), the RPT Note was substantially rewritten (similarity 1%), intercompany gross loan flows reached THB 86bn (increase) / THB 69bn (decrease) in 9M/68 on a net balance of THB 71.8bn — structurally opaque for RP size test purposes.
AWC.business: AWC is the flagship real estate and hospitality arm of TCC Group (Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi family), with TCC holding 74.97% via TCC Business Co. (44.98%) and TCC Retail Co. (29.99%). Business comprises: (1) Hotel — 51 hotels across Luxury, Upscale, and Midscale; (2) Commercial — retail malls, office, and mixed-use; (3) Food & Beverage — EA Rooftop and tenant F&B ecosystem. TCC ecosystem related parties include ThaiBev, BJC, Big C, QSR of Asia, Oishi, TCC Technology, Frasers Property Thailand, and Univentures.

sixThemes.preCb: Yellow. IBD/E 0.87x is manageable and within covenant comfort. Avg maturity 3.2 years and avg cost 2.54% reflect well-laddered debt. Risk is the ~THB 71.8bn intercompany standalone loan position — if subsidiaries experience stress, AWC standalone liquidity may be pressured (OPPDAY-AWC-2026-05-14-2026Q1.md; AWC-RPT-2026-05-17.md).
sixThemes.salesQuality: Yellow. Underlying hotel and commercial revenue growth (+12%, +16%) is genuine and recurring. However, THB 1,522mn FV gain (76.6% of NP) is non-recurring and represents a one-time uplift. Reported NP must be normalized by investors; headline EPS is misleading without this adjustment. ROFO/ROFR non-exercise means pipeline growth depends on organic development or external M&A rather than intra-group asset acquisition.
sixThemes.costMargin: Green-Yellow. Normalized EBITDA margin stable at ~30%+ on operating revenue. Hotel segment benefits from RevPAR growth without proportional cost increase. Commercial occupancy and tenant mix driving margin expansion (+35% Retail EBITDA). No significant cost spike noted. Key risk: FV methodology change could create FV reversal in future quarters.
sixThemes.workingCapital: Green. OCF THB 1,972.5mn in Q1/2026 is strong relative to reported NP and approximately in line with normalized EBITDA. Hotel and commercial businesses have relatively stable receivables cycles. No inventory-financing stress. Working capital cycle is service-business oriented and does not exhibit cash conversion cycle concerns.
sixThemes.cashFunding: Yellow. Capex THB 7,000mn/year requires consistent access to capital markets. Avg maturity 3.2 years is adequate but must be actively managed. The ~THB 71.8bn intercompany loan book creates opacity around AWC standalone cash needs. If TCC parent entities draw on ROFO/ROFR opportunities not pursued by AWC, future asset pipeline depends on third-party M&A (higher cost).
sixThemes.outlook: Neutral-positive on operations. Hotel and commercial momentum is real; RevPAR and Retail EBITDA trends suggest continued organic growth in Q2/Q3. Governance and RPT pre-assessment for ทจ.46/2568 are the critical deliverables before 1 July 2026. The FV gain methodology and its sustainability remain unresolved analyst questions. FY2026 normalized EBITDA growth is likely positive barring macro reversal.

AXTRART.name: AXTRA FUTURE CITY FREEHOLD AND LEASEHOLD REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST
AXTRART.thesis: AXTRART's Q1/69 recurring income is broadly stable (net profit on investments THB 536.4mn, -3.7% QoQ, -3.7% YoY) but the headline net assets from operations fell 47.1% YoY due to a THB 454.6mn FV swing (Q4/25 FV gain unwound) — occupancy range 89.6–99.2% across the 23 Lotus's mall portfolio is the key quality anchor, pending disclosure of a blended figure and WAULT.
AXTRART.summary: AXTRART was established in September 2024 through conversion of Lotus's Retail Growth Freehold and Leasehold Property Fund (LPF), with assets transferred November 2024. The Trust holds interests in 23 Lotus's shopping centres and 1 Life Xpress convenience store. Q1/69 revenue was THB 716.0mn with net profit on investments of THB 536.4mn (-3.7% YoY vs THB 557.1mn Q1/68; -2.0% QoQ vs THB 547.3mn Q4/68). Net assets from operations were THB 529.5mn vs THB 1,001.8mn Q4/68 and THB 556.6mn Q1/68 — the sharp decline reflects absence of the Q4/25 FV revaluation gain (THB 454.6mn) and an accounting policy change in Q4/25 (utility income reclassified to other income). Finance costs fell 12.4% QoQ to THB 21.7mn — suggesting conservative leverage. The 89.6–99.2% average occupancy range (valuation assumptions from FS Note) reflects a diversified portfolio across Lotus's anchor-tenant retail. Key open items: no health check in vault (AXTRART coverage note is a scraper stub), limited financial detail from the auto-ingest MD&A, and no disclosed DPU or NAV/unit for Q1/69 in vault sources.
AXTRART.business: REIT holding freehold and leasehold interests in 23 Lotus's shopping centres and 1 Life Xpress store; established Sep 2024 from LPF conversion; primary income is rental income and service fees from Lotus's Retail (CP group); 29.7bn THB market cap.
financialSnapshot: Q1/69: revenue THB 716.0mn; net profit on investments THB 536.4mn (-3.7% YoY); finance costs THB 21.7mn (-12.4% QoQ); net assets from operations THB 529.5mn (-4.9% YoY, -47.1% QoQ — QoQ swing driven by absent Q4/25 FV gain) (MDA_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Revenue/Profit Drivers).
Occupancy range (valuation assumption): 89.6–99.2% (31 Mar 2026 and 31 Dec 2025); expected market rental growth 3.0%; discount rate 9.5–10.5% (NOTES_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Segment/Revenue Evidence).
True Distribution & Sales Co. Ltd.: THB 3,127k in related-party transactions (NOTES_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Accounting/FS Note Flags).
FY revenue (9M proxy): THB 2,957.7mn (inspect.py dashboard); market price THB 12.70 (-3.79% YTD); PBV 1.01x; yield 7.44%; mcap THB 29.7bn.
Auditor: AUDITOR_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md — unqualified opinion (inferred from filing context).
mdaSynthesis: Q1/69 net profit on investments THB 536.4mn vs THB 557.1mn Q1/68 (-3.7% YoY) and THB 547.3mn Q4/68 (-2.0% QoQ) — modest decline; management cites reduced occupancy and decreased partnership-related income (MDA_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Revenue Drivers).

Q4/68 net assets from operations THB 1,001.8mn was elevated by FV gains (THB 454.6mn); absent in Q1/69 (FV loss THB 6.9mn) — this is the sole driver of the -47.1% QoQ swing in net assets from operations (MDA_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Net Gain/Loss on Investments).

Accounting policy change Q4/25: utility income reclassified to other income; QoQ other income -36.4% in Q1/69 reflects absence of a one-time THB 11.5mn Q4/25 write-off adjustment (MDA_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Risks/Watch).
Finance costs THB 21.7mn Q1/69 vs THB 24.7mn Q1/68 (+12.4% improvement) — positive signal on refinancing or deleveraging.
Renovation works in progress to enhance revenue-generating capability; completion timeline not specified (MDA_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Overview).

Occupancy (valuation assumption used in FV model): 89.6–99.2% range — no single blended figure reported; open item for IR (NOTES_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Segment/Revenue Evidence).

FS Note 3 covers related parties; Note 4 FV of freehold/leasehold properties; Note 8 right-of-use assets / lease liabilities — note 15 covers post-balance-sheet events (NOTES_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Source Excerpt).
Rental and service receivables: credit terms 7 days; ECL disclosure present — receivable quality appears standard (NOTES_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Segment/Revenue Evidence).
No material changes to related-party relationships or pricing since FY2025 annual FS (NOTES_AXTRART_2026Q1_E.md §Accounting Flags).

sixThemes.preCb: Green (inferred). Finance costs THB 21.7mn/quarter implies modest IBD; no debenture maturity information in vault. AXTRART is a newly converted trust (Sep 2024) with low legacy debt from LPF conversion structure.
sixThemes.salesQuality: Yellow. Occupancy range 89.6–99.2% is acceptable for a multi-property retail REIT, but blended figure and WAULT undisclosed. Related-party income decline (THB 10,922k Q1/68 to THB 1,044k Q1/69) requires explanation — may reflect end of LPF-to-REIT transition revenue.
sixThemes.costMargin: Adequate. Net profit on investments margin ~74.9% (THB 536.4mn ÷ THB 716mn revenue) — reasonable for a gross-lease retail REIT with Lotus's anchor.
sixThemes.workingCapital: Green (inferred). 7-day credit terms; ECL disclosure standard; receivable collection appears normal.
sixThemes.cashFunding: Green (inferred). Finance costs low at THB 21.7mn (-12.4% YoY); LTV and IBD not confirmed but structural leverage appears conservative for a newly-converted trust.
sixThemes.outlook: Neutral. Lotus's retail anchor provides stable occupancy (89.6–99.2%) and rental growth (3.0% modelled). Renovation pipeline is an upside catalyst. Risk: CP group / Lotus's related-party income normalisation post-conversion, and uncertainty about DPU sustainability without disclosed distributable income figure.

BTG.name: BETAGRO PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
BTG.thesis: BTG's Q1/2026 earnings collapsed 47% YoY as swine and poultry commodity cycles turned sharply negative, compressing GPM by 280bps while a THB 4,000mn dual-bond maturity (BTG26525A due 24 May 2026 + BTG267A due 28 Jul 2026) created an acute near-term refinancing test; RPT detail is unavailable from a binary-PDF FS notes extract, creating a source gap that must be resolved before ทจ.46/2568 effective date.
BTG.summary: BTG reported Q1/2026 (Q1/69) revenue of THB 28,561mn (−6.4% YoY) and net profit of THB 1,003mn (−47.1% YoY), with GPM declining to 14.8% from 17.6% a year ago. The collapse in swine and poultry prices — domestic Thai cycle — is the primary earnings driver. Pet food was the sole segment delivering YoY growth and partially cushioning margin. SG&A/revenue widened 50bps to 10.8% on operating leverage. IBD/E rose to 0.64x (from 0.58x at FY2025) amid the bond wall. EBITDA margin held at 9.5%, preserving some debt-service buffer. The critical watch item for IS1 is the bond maturity: BTG26525A (THB 2,000mn, due 24 May 2026) and BTG267A (THB 2,000mn, due 28 Jul 2026) represent THB 4,000mn of near-term redemptions out of THB 9,000mn total IBD. RPT analysis is blocked by binary-PDF FS notes — this is an open source gap requiring direct IR engagement before 1 Jul 2026.
BTG.business: Fully integrated agri-food conglomerate: (1) swine farming and pork processing, (2) poultry farming and chicken processing, (3) pet food manufacturing (growing segment), (4) food ingredients and distribution. Operates across Thailand with selected CLMV presence (Cambodia, Laos, Singapore expansion ongoing). Family and holding vehicles hold approximately 65.76% of shares. Rated bond issuer; bonds listed on Thai BEX.

CBG.name: CARABAO GROUP PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
CBG.thesis: CBG's Q1/2026 headline profit decline of 20% YoY reflects three intersecting stresses — a structural Cambodia CLMV revenue collapse (−41% YoY from border tensions), a transitional tax rate spike from overseas subsidiary startups, and a related-party purchase concentration of THB 2,271mn (16.1% of NTA) from an unidentified counterparty that will require full Large RPT disclosure under ทจ.46/2568; the core Thai beverage franchise (GPM 43%) and conservative balance sheet (D/E 0.38x) provide a resilience floor.
CBG.summary: CBG reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 5,321–5,374mn (−0.1% YoY) and net profit of THB 611mn (−19.7% YoY). The flat revenue masks a deep CLMV segment deterioration: Cambodia was −41% YoY from cross-border logistics disruptions, partially offset by Vietnam +96% (new distributor channel) and Myanmar factory ramp-up. The Thai beverage segment (49% of revenue) maintained GPM ~43% while Beer distribution (47% of revenue, GPM 9%) weighed on blended margins. Admin expenses surged +39% YoY from reclassification of overseas subsidiary startup costs (flagged as non-recurring). The effective tax rate elevated to 24% (vs normal ~20%) from overseas startup losses ineligible for consolidation tax credit — management guided this will normalise. RPT is the lead IS1 watchpoint: purchases from 'related by shareholders/directors' of THB 2,271mn in Q1/2026 = 16.1% of NTA, and sales to same RP of THB 425mn = 3.01% — both are Large RPT under ทจ.46/2568; counterparty identity was not disclosed in the FS notes. AR from RP of THB 895mn includes THB 28.6mn overdue 3–6 months (+79.5% QoQ spike). TRIS rating A/Stable. Share buyback THB 2,000mn announced (25 May – 24 Nov 2026).
CBG.business: CBG operates two principal business streams: (1) Energy drink manufacturing and brand management — Carabao brand (~49% of consolidated revenue), targeting Thailand and CLMV/export markets with GPM ~43%; (2) Beer and beverage distribution — distribution of Carabao and third-party beer brands (~47% of revenue), a high-volume low-margin segment (GPM 9%). Myanmar factory is in ramp-up phase. Vietnam and Cambodia represent key CLMV growth markets. Family control through Yutichai family and related vehicles.

mdaSynthesis: Cambodia CLMV revenue −41% YoY — management attributed to border logistics tensions between Thailand and Cambodia disrupting cross-border distribution chains; this is a structural channel disruption, not a demand issue, and the timeline for recovery is uncertain (MDA_CBG_2026Q1_T.md).

Vietnam +96% YoY from new distributor appointment — high base-effect growth; sustainability depends on distributor execution; Q2 will be the first full-quarter test of the new channel (MDA_CBG_2026Q1_T.md).

Myanmar factory operational and ramping — startup losses are being expensed; this is the primary driver of both admin cost +39% YoY and elevated tax rate 24% (overseas sub not yet generating taxable profit to offset). Management guided that admin normalises once Myanmar reaches breakeven (MDA_CBG_2026Q1_T.md).
Thai domestic beverage segment stable to slightly soft — no volume growth disclosed for Q1/2026; the core Carabao brand maintained pricing and distribution (MDA_CBG_2026Q1_T.md).

Share buyback THB 2,000mn announced 25 May 2026 running to 24 Nov 2026 — signals management confidence in cashflow but will reduce free float and potentially affect Large RPT vote quorum (Health Check CBG.md).

Under ทจ.46/2568 this requires board approval + SET disclosure + shareholder vote + IFA opinion before or after 1 Jul 2026 depending on transaction date (NOTES_CBG_2026Q1_T.md; CBG-RPT-2026-05-18.md).

CFRESH.name: SEAFRESH INDUSTRY PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
CFRESH.thesis: CFRESH returned to profit in Q1/2026 (+THB 30.1mn) after a loss year, but the recovery rests on thin gross margins (12.9%) under structural pressure from shrimp input-cost competition with India/Vietnam/Ecuador, a high D/E (0.94x), and an unresolved THB 971mn receivable/loan from the illiquid Belize Aquaculture JV that cannot be collected on demand.
CFRESH.summary: Q1/2026 revenue was THB 1,827.7mn vs the FY/2025 quarterly average of ~THB 1,988mn, suggesting continuing top-line softness. Net profit attributable recovered to THB 30.1mn (NPM 2.5%), against a full-year FY/2025 net of only THB 28.8mn and a FY/2024 net loss of THB -81.5mn. The improvement is real but fragile: gross margin at 12.9% compares with 12.6% FY/2025 and 13.2% FY/2024, indicating no structural recovery in processing economics. The KAM in the FY/2025 auditor report is inventory valuation — raw shrimp is priced against India and Ecuador competitors who benefit from lower input costs, limiting CFRESH's ability to pass through cost increases. The balance sheet carries THB 972mn in net receivables/loans to Belize Aquaculture Limited (a JV within the SGH UK cluster), where interest income has not been accrued since 2016 — this is a non-cash dormant asset with no near-term recovery mechanism. Director-linked and connected-person borrowings (Narit Chia-Apar THB 70mn + Thai K. Boiler THB 12.8mn at Q1/2025) plus a Temchu Limited loan of THB 71mn represent layered RPT obligations. D/E 0.94x vs current ratio 1.34x — adequate but not comfortable. A new CFO was appointed 1 April 2026; the dividend was omitted for FY/2025.
CFRESH.business: Manufactures and distributes frozen shrimp and seafood products primarily for export (~90% foreign revenue). Key markets: US, EU, Japan, Canada, Australia. Brands: Seafresh, Sea Angel, Go-Go. Subsidiary cluster: Sea Farms Inc. (US), SGH UK cluster, Fin Meals Europe Limited (est. Feb 2025 for EU expansion), Seafresh Gourmet, Hia-jia Gourmet (domestic restaurant/franchise). Headquartered in Chumphon. FY/2025 revenue THB 7,950mn.

CHOTI.thesis: CHOTI is in active balance-sheet distress: FY/2025 booked a THB -428mn net loss driven by a THB 375mn flood-damage provision, D/E has surged to 4.57x in Q1/2026, the current ratio fell below 1.0x (0.84x), OCF is deeply negative at THB -74.3mn for Q1/2026, and a subsidiary guarantee of THB 709mn (~57% of NTA) becomes a Large RPT requiring shareholder approval under ทจ. 46/2568 effective 1 Jul 2026.
CHOTI.summary: CHOTI (Kiang Huat Sea Gull) operates frozen seafood and cold storage in Hat Yai (Songkhla). A catastrophic November 2025 flood forced production shutdown; the company restarted in January 2026 with a new cold-storage facility (Food Futures Co., Ltd., 99.99% subsidiary). Q1/2026 revenue was THB 530.5mn — the first full-quarter post-restart — but net loss continued at THB -18.1mn (NPM -3.4%). GPM recovered to 5.0% from FY/2025's disaster-distorted -11.9%. D/E exploded to 4.57x as the company drew on long-term loans to fund the THB 468mn cold-storage rebuild (Food Futures PPE). Insurance compensation for the THB 375mn flood loss had not been recognised as of FY/2025 and its Q1/2026 status is unconfirmed. The 99.99%-owned Food Futures gets the >=90% exemption from ทจ. 46/2568 for intercompany transactions, but the THB 709mn external bank guarantee that CHOTI provides for Food Futures' borrowings requires fresh legal analysis — it is an off-balance-sheet obligation that likely constitutes a Large RPT (57% NTA) and requires shareholder approval. A director change was also filed in April 2026. The MDA Q1/2026 was not fully extracted from raw PDF; several figures in this report are inferred from prior periods.
CHOTI.business: Produces and exports frozen seafood (shrimp, squid, fish) and frozen fruit (~85% USD-invoiced exports to US, EU, Japan). Also operates Food Futures Company Limited (99.99%), a cold-storage and frozen-fruit production subsidiary. Associate: Kiang Huat Seagull Trading Frozen Food Sdn. Bhd. (Malaysia, 40%). FY/2025 revenue THB 2,435.7mn.

sixThemes.outlook: Positive. Central Chiangmai Airport final phase completion (expected 2026) adds incremental occupancy; MPC rate cut 25bps to 1.00% (Feb 2026) improves refinancing spread. Main risk is macro consumer spending slowdown and Hilton sub-lessee uncertainty.

FTREIT.name: FRASERS PROPERTY THAILAND INDUSTRIAL FREEHOLD & LEASEHOLD REIT
FTREIT.thesis: FTREIT is the highest-quality industrial REIT in the IS1 coverage — net lease NPI margin 91.7%, interest coverage 8.50x, LTV 27.4% (best headroom in peer set) — but two near-term items need resolution: the THB 1,200mn debenture wall due June–August 2026 and the expired common service agreement with FPT group.
FTREIT.summary: Q1/69 (3M ended Mar 2026, FTREIT's Q3 of FY ending Sep 2026) saw recurring net profit on investment grow 9.8% YoY to THB 770.6mn on rental income of THB 1,110.7mn (+5.8% YoY), with NPI margin expanding to 91.7% (+1.9pp YoY) as the net-lease structure passes operating costs to tenants. The headline FV loss of THB 79.3mn compressed reported net assets from operations by 22.6% YoY to THB 691.3mn — this is a non-cash revaluation, not operating deterioration. DPU for the period was THB 0.1950/unit (+3.7% YoY), continuing a consistent upward trend of 3–4% per quarter. Portfolio GFA is now 2.37mn sqm across 30+ buildings after two Q1/69 acquisitions from sponsor FPT (Asia IE Suvarnabhumi THB 218.8mn + Eastern Seaboard 1B THB 235.9mn). LTV of 27.4% vs the 60% covenant cap gives 32.6pp of headroom — the most in the peer set. Key governance item: the common service agreement with FPT group expired December 2025 and has not been formally renewed; and EGM + IFA documentation for the two Q1/69 acquisitions needs verification before the 1 July 2026 regulatory deadline.
FTREIT.business: Freehold and leasehold REIT holding 2.37mn sqm GFA of warehouses and factories across 30+ locations in EEC, Ayutthaya, Samut Prakan and other industrial clusters; net-lease structure; sponsor and REIT Manager both in the Frasers Property Thailand (FPT) group; Trustee BBLAM (Bangkok Bank group, independent).

DPU Q3/69 THB 0.1950/unit (+3.7% YoY); annualised DPU THB 0.7800/unit; DPU trend +3–4% per quarter for 5 quarters (MDA_FTREIT_2026Q1_T.md §DPU; FTREIT.md HC v1.0 Theme 3).
LTV 27.4% (IBD THB 14,687mn / total assets THB 53,541mn); headroom 32.6pp to 60% cap; interest coverage 8.50x; unutilised credit THB 2,900mn (FTREIT.md HC v1.0 Theme 4).

NAV/unit THB 11.2226; units outstanding 3,283,387k; portfolio FV subject to 6M partial revaluation (loss THB 229.3mn 6M/69 vs gain THB 138.4mn 6M/68) — non-cash (MDA_FTREIT_2026Q1_T.md §F45 clarification FIRM 008/2026).

mdaSynthesis: Recurring income growth confirmed by FIRM 008/2026 (F45 clarification): recurring net profit +9.8% Q1/69 driven by (1) higher occupancy and new assets from FY2025 and Q1/69 acquisitions, (2) cost of rent -13.3% YoY on better maintenance management (MDA_FTREIT_2026Q1_T.md §1).

Headline net assets from operations decline (-22.6% YoY Q1/69) entirely attributable to FV revaluation loss (THB 79.3mn) vs FV gain in Q1/68 (THB 191.7mn) — management explicitly distinguishes recurring vs non-recurring in the FIRM 008/2026 letter (MDA_FTREIT_2026Q1_T.md §1).

Finance cost +6.4% YoY to THB 119.7mn reflects additional debt for acquisitions; trust management fee +7.4% YoY to THB 134.3mn (single 6M figure) tracks income growth — both cited as recurring headwinds in FIRM 008/2026.

Rental guarantee income THB 4.6mn from FPT (Q1/68: nil) — non-recurring, related to newly acquired properties during ramp-up; other income THB 12.3mn (+4x YoY, unexplained) is a watch item (MDA_FTREIT_2026Q1_T.md §Other income).

Post-period: new debenture 1/2026 issued 3 Apr 2026 for THB 1,000mn (5Y at 2.80%, 7Y at 3.35%) — reduces the net maturity wall and locks in lower rates vs older vintage bonds at 4.06–4.19% (FTREIT.md HC v1.0 Theme 4).
fsNotesSynthesis: Asset acquisitions from FPT group: Asia IE Suvarnabhumi THB 218.8mn (28 Nov 2025) and Eastern Seaboard 1B THB 235.9mn (18 Dec 2025) — total THB 454.7mn = 1.24% of NAV; EGM + IFA documentation for both must be verified (NOTES_FTREIT_2026Q1_T.md Note 9; FTREIT-RPT-2026-05-17.md §4).

Debenture maturity wall: FTREIT274A THB 700mn due 24 Jun 2026; FTREIT268A THB 500mn due 8 Aug 2026; short-term borrowings THB 1,100mn due Apr–May 2026 — total THB 2,300mn pre-refi, reduced to ~THB 1,200mn after Apr 2026 debenture issuance (NOTES_FTREIT_2026Q1_T.md Notes 6–7; ThaiBMA snapshot 2026-05-12).

Common service agreement with FPT group expired December 2025 — REIT operating in interim mode for 3+ months without formal contract renewal; both TM-T 2/2566 (REIT side) and ทจ.46/2568 (FPT side) frameworks must be in place before 1 Jul 2026 (FTREIT.md HC v1.0 Theme 5).
Berli Jucker Logistics tenant rent THB 46.3mn 6M (+12.9% YoY) — RP tenant; BJ group % unitholding in FTREIT needs verification for connected-person test (FTREIT-RPT-2026-05-17.md §3).

Trustee: BBLAM (Bangkok Bank group) confirmed independent from FPT/Frasers — sole independent check in a structure where both REIT Manager and Property Manager are FPT subsidiaries (FTREIT-RPT-2026-05-17.md §2).

sixThemes.preCb: Green. Investment-grade access confirmed; new THB 1,000mn debenture issued at 2.80–3.35% in Apr 2026 below prior vintage rates. LTV 27.4% vs 60% cap, coverage 8.50x.
sixThemes.salesQuality: Yellow. Rental income quality is strong (net lease, +5.8% YoY) but actual occupancy and WAULT are not reported in interim FS — the two critical metrics for assessing lease expiry risk remain open items from IR.
sixThemes.costMargin: Green. NPI margin 91.7% (+1.9pp YoY) reflects net-lease cost pass-through; direct costs fell 13.3% YoY on maintenance savings. Trust management fee 1.47% of NAV is below CPNREIT (1.98% incl. property mgmt).
sixThemes.workingCapital: Green. Net-lease structure minimises working-capital complexity; rental guarantee income from FPT supports ramp-up assets.
sixThemes.cashFunding: Yellow. FTREIT274A THB 700mn due 24 Jun 2026 is 6 weeks away from health-check date; FTREIT268A THB 500mn due Aug 2026. Both require active refinancing. LTV headroom (32.6pp) and unutilised THB 2,900mn credit provide substantial liquidity buffer.
sixThemes.outlook: Positive. DPU growth trend (+3–4%/quarter) backed by income growth and low LTV leaves significant acquisition dry powder. EEC industrial demand from China+1 FDI and logistics secular growth support occupancy. Risks: common service agreement lapse, FPT sponsor pipeline dependent on FPT parent health.

HPF.summary: HPF is a closed-end property fund (no REIT conversion) holding freehold rights to 47 factory units (95,941 sqm) and leasehold rights to 57 factory units (54,176 sqm) in Hemaraj-WHA industrial estates in Rayong, Chonburi and Saraburi. Q1/69 rental and service income was THB 82.3mn (+4.4% YoY from THB 78.9mn Q1/68) — a modest but positive trend. FV change on investments was a gain of THB 40mn in Q1/69 vs loss of THB 4mn Q4/68; the appraisal was performed in 2025 by Assetasia Corporation. The fund has been systematically returning capital: registered capital has been reduced 7 times from THB 4,700mn (Feb 2017) to THB 4,321mn (May 2023), with NAV per unit declining correspondingly. As a property fund (not REIT), HPF falls under PF-specific regulations rather than TM-T 2/2566 for REITs, though the WHA property management agreement (10-year term, 25 Dec 2013 to 24 Dec 2023) has formally expired and the continuation basis is unconfirmed — this is the principal governance flag. No acquisition pipeline exists for a closed-end PF nearing maturity.

OCF THB 1,026mn = 3.6x NP — exceptional cash conversion for a branded beverage company. D/E 0.21x, current ratio 3.55x. The export segment declined −72.7% YoY due to Thai-Cambodia border closure disrupting cross-border logistics, while Thai domestic revenue grew +16.4% YoY. Admin costs +33.2% YoY are a watch item. The key RPT resolution: DKSH (Thailand) Co., Ltd. — ICHI's major customer representing 90.7% of Q1/2026 revenue (THB 1,749.5mn) — was confirmed as a THIRD PARTY (not RP) via 56-1 Y68 review, eliminating the largest conditional Large RPT risk. ITC.thesis: ITC delivered the strongest quarter in the IS1 coverage universe — revenue +21.8% YoY (USD +28.6%), NP +28.7%, pet treats +95% YoY — with all-geography growth, a structural shift to premium mix (51.5%), and 2026 guidance on track; the sole priority is the TU group Large RPT (764.5mn = 3.14% NTA) requiring board framework approval before 1 Jul 2026, while Pillar 2 GMT (5-7% ETR) is a manageable structural headwind.

Pet treats 1,076mn (+95% YoY — structural growth confirmed), dog food +44.6%, cat food +4.0%. Americas +59.5% YoY, Europe +49.2% YoY. Premium mix 51.5% of revenue. Private label 21.3% (US Chunk & Pate platform). 2026 guidance: USD +9-12%, GPM 23-25%, SGA/sales 9-10%, capex 1bn THB — all on track. TU parent (79.30%) group aggregate Q1/69 RPT = 764.5mn = 3.14% NTA = Large RPT (confirmed). Subsidiary loans 1,373mn: exemption status depends on holding % — ≥90% → exempt, <90% → Large RPT. Pillar 2 GMT increasing ETR from ~1% to 5-7% — Q1/69 actual step-up 17.4mn. ITC tariff 19% vs TU 10% (HS code structural difference) — ITC-specific exposure managed via direct US sales platform.
ITC.business: Thailand's leading pet food manufacturer and exporter. Subsidiary of TU (Thai Union Group, 79.30% holding). Segments: (1) dog food (~40% revenue), (2) cat food (~35%), (3) pet treats (~20%, fastest growing), (4) other pet nutrition products. US and Europe are primary export markets (~70%+ of revenue). Private label platform 21.3% (US retail chains). TU group purchasing relationships (ingredients, packaging) are primary RPT vector. BOI-privileged manufacturing.

mdaSynthesis: Pet treats structural growth: 1,076mn (+95% YoY) — driven by US and European premiumization trend; management views this as structural, not cyclical. Portfolio expansion into new treat formats (dental, functional) is underway (MDA_ITC_2026Q1_E.md).

Americas +59.5% YoY, Europe +49.2% YoY — broad-based geographic growth; Asia contribution growing but smaller base. Private label Chunk & Pate US platform at 21.3% represents strategic distribution breadth (MDA_ITC_2026Q1_E.md).

Tariff exposure: ITC at 19% US tariff rate vs TU at 10% — HS code structural difference means ITC-specific exposure; management strategy is to accelerate direct-to-US-retail sales platform to reduce tariff sensitivity over time (MDA_ITC_2026Q1_E.md).

Pillar 2 GMT step-up: Q1/69 actual incremental tax 17.4mn from global minimum tax; FY2026 guidance implies ETR 5-7% vs prior ~1% — cumulative NP impact ~270-420mn per year at current NP run-rate (Health Check ITC Q1/69).

If any subsidiary is <90% held → that portion = Large RPT. Exact holding % per subsidiary not confirmed in vault (ITC-RPT-2026-05-17.md).

Pillar 2 GMT: ITC is subject to global minimum tax at 15% due to international operations exceeding revenue thresholds. ETR guided to 5-7% FY2026 vs prior ~1% from BOI privileges — significant structural change. Q1/69 actual step-up 17.4mn recognized (Health Check ITC Q1/69).
Premium mix 51.5%: more than half of revenue now from premium products — supports GPM target range 23-25%; favorable mix shift de-risks GPM guidance (MDA_ITC_2026Q1_E.md).

ITC private label 21.3%: US Chunk & Pate and equivalent European platforms provide revenue stability via long-term retailer contracts; branded mix at 78.7% (including own brands) maintains pricing premium (MDA_ITC_2026Q1_E.md).

sixThemes.salesQuality: Green. Revenue +21.8% YoY broad-based (all geographies, all major segments). Premium mix improving. Private label provides recurring revenue floor. No non-recurring revenue inflation — USD revenue +28.6% confirms currency-neutral strength.

sixThemes.workingCapital: Yellow. OCF 379.4mn vs NP 871mn = OCF/NP 0.44x — below 1.0x in Q1, suggesting working capital absorption from revenue growth (higher AR, inventory build for expansion). Monitoring needed for Q2 to confirm OCF recovery as revenue growth moderates to steady state.

sixThemes.outlook: Positive. Pet treats +95% YoY growth is the strongest structural driver in IS1 FOOD coverage. Americas and Europe all-weather growth. 2026 guidance conservatively set (USD +9-12% vs Q1 run-rate +28.6%). RPT framework and Pillar 2 GMT are the two governance/tax watch items but neither threatens the fundamental earnings trajectory.

LH.name: LAND AND HOUSES PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
LH.thesis: LH's earnings are structurally dependent on associate income (HMPRO/QH/LHFG providing 117% of operating profit in Q1/2026), RE GPM collapsed to 13.3% (half the normal level), and three HIGH-severity RPT items under ทจ. 46/2568 — LHBANK deposits 5,180mn, Reco Resorts loan 418mn, and the LHHOTEL comfort letter expiring 14 Jun 2026 (17 days before the new rules take effect) — demand immediate resolution alongside the 27,600mn bond wall.
LH.summary: LH Q1/2026 net profit (attributable) was THB 695mn, down 17.0% YoY, on total revenues THB 5,007mn (-0.5%). Real estate transfer revenue fell 20.5% YoY to THB 2,131mn — Q1 pace covers only 50% of the implied FY2026 quarterly run-rate on the 17,000mn transfer target — with GPM of just 13.3% vs 26.1% a year ago, the most anomalous margin in the peer group. The hotel segment offset with +34.2% YoY revenue to 2,135mn driven by the Grande Centre Point Prestige Ratchadamri opening (509 rooms). OCF turned positive at +1,118mn vs Q1/2025's -81mn, a welcome reversal. However, associate income (811mn) exceeds standalone operating profit (EBIT 365mn), making LH's consolidated P&L heavily dependent on HMPRO, QH, and LHFG — two of which (QH at 8,480mn carrying vs 3,666mn market value; LHFG at 9,203mn vs 4,681mn market) show significant impairment indicators that have not been tested in the interim FS. The bond wall is the sector's largest: THB 27,600mn (62% of outstanding) within 12 months — partially addressed by a 6,000mn issuance on 13 May 2026 but still substantial. Three Large RPT items require SH approval frameworks before 1 Jul 2026.
LH.business: Residential property developer (detached houses, townhouses, condos) with 69 active projects across Bangkok and provinces; revenue now split equally between real estate and hotels. Hotel arm operates Grande Centre Point chain (incl. Prestige Ratchadamri 509 keys opened Q1/2026; Voyage Pattaya 494 keys planned Q4/2026). Associate web includes HMPRO (~24%), QH (~24%), LHFG (financial group), LHHOTEL (REIT), QCP, LHPF-II. Subsidiary LHSC manages commercial properties and LHRREIT.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 5,007mn (-0.5% YoY), net profit (attributable) 695mn (-17.0% YoY), NPM 13.8%; normalized NP ~644mn after netting non-recurring FX gain 265mn and derivatives loss (214mn) (HC LH.md Theme 3).
RE GPM 13.3% vs 26.1% Q1/2025 — anomalous compression likely from product mix shift and possibly inventory cost write-ups; hotel GPM 36.7% (+7.0pp YoY) on new hotel scale (HC LH.md Themes 2–3).
OCF +1,118mn (Q1/2025: -81mn) — strong reversal driven by 1,574mn inventory-to-COGS conversion; cash 6,139mn + undrawn 5,880mn at 31 Mar 2026 (HC LH.md Theme 4).

Total IBD 79,164mn (incl. TFRS16 lease liabilities 10,034mn); debentures outstanding THB 36,771mn; bond wall ≤12 months: 27,600mn (ThaiBMA 12 May 2026; 62% of bonds); LH issued 6,000mn new debentures 13 May 2026 to refinance part (MDA_LH_2026Q1_T.md).
Associate carrying values: HMPRO 9,345mn (FV 24,452mn = +162%); QH 8,480mn (FV 3,666mn = -57%); LHFG 9,203mn (FV 4,681mn = -49%) — QH and LHFG impairment indicators unresolved (HC LH.md Theme 5).
mdaSynthesis: Hotel segment pivoted to revenue parity with RE in Q1/2026: both at ~2,135mn. Grande Centre Point Prestige Ratchadamri (509 rooms, THB 4,600mn investment) opened in Q1/2026 — ramp-up still underway, GPM 36.7% is promising but occupancy and RevPAR not disclosed in interim FS (MDA_LH_2026Q1_T.md hotel section).

RE transfer pace critically below target: THB 2,131mn in Q1 vs implied quarterly average of 4,250mn for 17,000mn FY2026 target — requires acceleration in Q2–Q4, and inventory pipeline (69 projects / 80,000mn value) must convert faster (MDA_LH_2026Q1_T.md real estate section).

FX gain THB 265mn from USD assets (LH USA Inc.) and derivatives loss (214mn) net to +51mn non-recurring — normalized Q1 NP approximately 644mn vs 837mn Q1/2025 (-23% YoY normalized) (HC LH.md Theme 3).

Associates contribution: HMPRO 424mn + QH 116mn + LHFG 184mn + LHHOTEL 59mn + QCP 11mn + LHPF-II 16mn = 810mn total — this exceeds EBIT of 365mn; LH's standalone RE business lost 323mn at operating level in Q1/2026 (HC LH.md Themes 2–3).

Inventory overhang building: DIO 1,473 days FY2025 (up from 1,216 days FY2024, 1,033 days FY2023) — three consecutive years of lengthening working capital cycle, a structural concern for cash conversion (HC LH.md Theme 4).
fsNotesSynthesis: LHBANK deposits: consolidated 5,180mn at 31 Mar 2026 (separate basis 4,082mn) — LHFG (LHBANK parent) is an associate → Related Person under ทจ. 46/2568; size test 5,180/52,960 = 9.8% of NA = Large RPT threshold (3% = 1,589mn); board-approved framework must be in place before 1 Jul 2026 or SH approval required (LH-RPT-2026-05-17.md HIGH-1).

LHHOTEL comfort letter for Grande Centre Point Ratchadamri sublease expires 14 Jun 2026 — LHHOTEL is an associate → RP; renewal or new arrangement after 1 Jul 2026 would be a Large RPT requiring IFA + SH vote; critical 17-day gap between expiry (14 Jun) and effective date of new rules (1 Jul) must be managed (LH-RPT-2026-05-17.md HIGH-2).

Reco Resorts Pte Ltd LT loan: 418mn (up +16.2mn QoQ) — classified as 'related company' in FS; special-case Large RPT (threshold: any amount ≥100mn for financial support to related company); ownership structure not yet confirmed from 56-1 Y68 (LH-RPT-2026-05-17.md HIGH-3).

QH carrying value 8,480mn vs market value 3,666mn (-57% discount) and LHFG 9,203mn vs 4,681mn (-49%): both exceed the carrying value — impairment indicators exist under TAS 28/TFRS; no interim impairment testing noted; combined potential overstatement ~9,000mn on BS (HC LH.md Theme 5).

Lease liabilities LHHOTEL (TFRS16): 5,245mn at 31 Mar 2026 (increased 516mn in Q1); right-of-use assets 22,577mn (18,077mn pledged as collateral); LHHOTEL sublease drives the hotel segment but the associated RP financial exposure is substantial (HC LH.md Theme 5).

sixThemes.preCb: MED. Equity 52,960mn is large; A/TRIS rating maintained; interest coverage 14.7x (on an annualized EBITDA proxy). However, the Asawabhokin family covenant clause in loan agreements means any family stake reduction could trigger event-of-default provisions — this is a structural governance-debt linkage worth monitoring. Meyland Co. Ltd (5.67% holder) relationship to Asawabhokin family unconfirmed (HC LH.md Theme 1).
sixThemes.salesQuality: HIGH concern. RE revenue 2,131mn represents 50% of the quarterly run-rate needed to hit FY2026 17,000mn target; presales breakdown not available from secondary sources; backlog estimated at ~9.25bn (InnovestX, needs verification from primary MD&A). The hotel offset is real but RE is the core business and it is underperforming materially. Rent revenue decline 42.7% YoY largely explained by prior-year REIT asset sales — partly mechanical (MDA_LH_2026Q1_T.md).
sixThemes.costMargin: MED-HIGH. RE GPM 13.3% is the most anomalous data point — normal range is 27–30%; root cause not explained in secondary-sourced MD&A; candidates are product mix (lower-margin condos), cost overruns, or inventory write-downs (tiny: 7.9mn reversal). Until root cause is explained, this flag stays elevated (HC LH.md Theme 3).
sixThemes.workingCapital: MED. OCF +1,118mn in Q1/2026 is a clear improvement, but DIO trending from 1,033 → 1,216 → 1,473 days over three years shows inventory absorption slowing. Cash 6,139mn + undrawn 5,880mn = adequate buffer but bond wall requires continuous refinancing execution (HC LH.md Theme 4).
sixThemes.cashFunding: HIGH. Bond wall THB 27,600mn (62% of outstanding) within 12 months is the largest in the peer group; partially offset by 6,000mn new issuance 13 May 2026; D/E target of 1.0x vs current 1.67x implies the company must accelerate RE transfers to reduce debt. IBD/EBITDA estimated ~7–9x (incl. lease liabilities). Covenant on Asawabhokin family stake is an additional binary risk (HC LH.md Theme 6).
sixThemes.outlook: Cautious. FY2026 RE transfer target 17,000mn requires a 2x acceleration from Q1's pace; hotel ramp-up is on track but only partially offsets. Two associates (QH, LHFG) are carried well above market value without interim impairment testing. RPT compliance is complex and urgent. Bond wall management is the dominant near-term risk.

M.name: MK RESTAURANT GROUP PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
M.thesis: MK Restaurant Group is printing structurally lower returns — Q1/2026 NPM 3.7% and ROE 5.7% versus 9.2% and 10.6% two years ago — as rising input costs and weak consumer purchasing power compress margins on a growing but lower-yielding branch base, and earnings quality requires verification against the full FS for RPT and branch-level segment detail.
M.summary: MK Restaurant Group (M) reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 4,098mn and net profit THB 163mn (NPM 3.7%), reflecting sustained cost pressure on what was historically a high-margin restaurant chain. Revenue from sales grew to THB 3,541mn (per MDA), with cost of sales rising 29.5% YoY to THB 1,538mn, squeezing gross profit to THB 2,509mn (+6.6% YoY) but driving GPM to 62.0% — still high in absolute terms but declining from the 67.4% of two years ago. The group operated 701 branches at 31 March 2026 (vs 689 at year-end 2025), indicating continued expansion of the MK Suki, Yayoi, and Laem Charoen brands. The MD&A cites logistics cost escalation, geopolitical oil price pressures, and weakened consumer purchasing power as the key headwinds. The auditor issued a clean TSRE 2410 review conclusion. OCF of THB 600mn in Q1 against net profit of THB 163mn implies a 3.7x OCF/NP ratio, likely reflecting depreciation of the significant lease portfolio. The long-term ROE erosion (from 10.6% in FY2024 to 5.7% in Q1/2026 annualized) and margin compression are the surveillance items; the FS notes contain a short-term loan to a related party that requires size-testing under ทจ. 46/2568.
M.business: Thailand's leading hot-pot restaurant operator: MK Suki (core brand, ~447 company branches), Bonus Suki, Yayoi (Japanese, franchise from Japan), Hikiniku to Come (franchise), Hakata, Miyazaki, Laem Charoen Seafood, and Na Siam. Operates 701 consolidated branches across Thailand and limited overseas operations. Revenue model is entirely restaurant-based with a production/distribution arm supplying group restaurants.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 4,098mn, net profit THB 163mn, NPM 3.7%, GPM 62.0%, D/E 0.43x, Current Ratio 2.66x, OCF THB 600mn (MDA_M_2026Q1_E.md; dashboard).

Revenue mix improving marginally — brand diversification (Yayoi, Laem Charoen, Na Siam) is adding revenue but these brands carry different cost structures from core MK Suki; management is expanding to attract new customer segments (MDA_M_2026Q1_E.md).

Consumer spending remains cautious: the MD&A cites Thai economic slowdown linked to US-Iran geopolitical tensions and oil price spikes as a demand dampener — a structural rather than temporary headwind for a mid-price restaurant operator (MDA_M_2026Q1_E.md).

MADAME.thesis: MADAME (formerly GLOCON) reported its first profitable Q1 in years (THB 21.5mn NP, NPM 5.4%) driven by a high-GPM skincare segment (Madame Louis, GPM 77.1%), but the CB designation (since March 2026) persists despite an AGM vote to clear accumulated losses, a covenant breach on LT loans is unwaived, OCF is negative, goodwill of THB 323mn (25% of total assets) carries impairment risk, and a ก.ล.ต. clarification request in May 2026 adds a regulatory overhang.
MADAME.summary: MADAME rebranded from GLOCON (effective 30 Jul 2025) to reflect its pivot from restaurant/packaging to skincare-led consumer health. Q1/2026 marks the first full quarter with Madame Louis skincare (acquired from Triton Resources for THB 150mn in May 2025) contributing THB 87.5mn revenue at a GPM of 77.1%. Consolidated GPM surged to 30.1% from a 5.9% comparable base (Q1/2025 had a THB 374mn non-recurring other-income item). Net profit THB 21.5mn — but OCF was negative at THB -27.6mn due to AR build (THB 44.9mn increase). The CB designation was issued 2 March 2026; AGM on 23 April 2026 voted to clear accumulated losses of THB 1,056mn via a capital reduction (par value 2.50 → 0.82 baht), creating a capital surplus that offsets the deficit — a non-cash accounting action that does not improve cash or debt-service capacity. A covenant breach on D/E and DSCR ratios is disclosed in Note 16 without a lender waiver. Goodwill of THB 323mn (Phong-Sra THB 241mn + Madame Louis THB 82mn) is 25.1% of total assets with a prior-year impairment on the Phong-Sra CGU. On 19 May 2026 MADAME filed a SET clarification regarding a ก.ล.ต. news release No.104/2026 — the nature of the SEC inquiry is the most critical governance open item.
MADAME.business: Three operating segments after portfolio restructuring: (1) Skincare — Madame Louis brand (premium collagen/skincare, acquired Q2/2025 from connected party Triton Resources); (2) Food — Phong-Sra Manufacturing/Distribution (processed meat products, 70% owned); (3) Packaging — Prompt Pac (plastic packaging, 95% owned). Subsidiaries being wound down: NPP Food Inc. (restaurant), Kitchen Plus Franchise, Fruity Bliss. Fruity Dry Co. Ltd sold Dec 2025. Target: Skincare revenue THB 450mn in 2026 growing to THB 2,000mn by 2030 (OPPDAY-MADAME-2026-05-21-2026Q1.md).

ORI.name: ORIGIN PROPERTY PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
ORI.thesis: Origin is a holding company with 5 listed/unlisted subsidiaries and 108 JV projects — the group structure creates complexity at the worst time: ORI267A (2,068mn) matures 10 Jul 2026 (28 days away), EBIT alone does not cover finance costs (coverage ~0.85x), and ORI's ownership of BRI has not been confirmed against the 90% RPT-exemption threshold under ทจ. 46/2568 effective 1 Jul 2026.
ORI.summary: ORI Q1/2026 revenue was THB 1,690mn (-2.2% YoY), net profit (attributable) THB 103.5mn (-7.3% YoY), EPS THB 0.042. The headline decline masks a significant improvement in RE GPM (30.1% vs 20.4% Q1/2025) from better project mix. However, share of JV profit collapsed 34.8% YoY to THB 168mn — the swing factor — as fewer high-margin JV condos transferred. Normalized NP stripping the THB 96.2mn one-off disposal gain (Origin Kata Phuket) is approximately THB 27mn, thin against THB 187mn quarterly finance costs. Presales of THB 4,511mn (condo 88% + BRI low-rise 12%) track 18% of the THB 25,000mn FY2026 target; backlog is THB 34,681mn (61% ready-to-move). The debt picture is improving (D/E down from 1.49x to 1.41x QoQ) but the absolute bond wall is acute: ORI267A (2,068mn, 10 Jul 2026) is only 28 days away, with ORI269A (715mn, 31 Aug 2026) close behind. The refinancing strategy — bank lines + JV/sub disposal proceeds — depends partly on the Ibis Phuket Kata sale closing in Q2/2026. RPT exposure includes: BRI (listed sub, ORI% unconfirmed vs 90% exemption), JV project management income (138mn/Q), and an MOU advance of 630mn for the Ibis Phuket Kata disposal. Excess equity method deficit rose 170mn QoQ to 380mn, signalling losses in some JVs exceeding invested capital.
ORI.business: Holding company over 5 business groups: (1) Origin Vertical — condo development (flagship); (2) Britania PCL (BRI, SET-listed) — low-rise housing; (3) Primo Service Solution PCL (PRI, SET-listed) — property services; (4) Origin Hotel PCL (SET-listed) — hospitality with 9 hotels / 2,306 keys / THB 13,800mn asset value; (5) Alpha Industrial Solution — logistics/warehouses (360,000 sqm, 97% occupancy). JV portfolio: 108 active projects with Nomura Real Estate as largest partner (12+ JVs), plus Lofis Thailand, GS E&C, Sotetsu, and others. FY2026 new launch target: 19,400mn (residential + hotel + office + warehouse).
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue 1,690mn (-2.2% YoY), NP attributable 103.5mn (-7.3%), NPM 6.1%; normalized NP stripping disposal gain ~96mn ≈ THB 27mn (MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md Tables I, IV).

RE GPM improved to 30.1% (from 20.4% Q1/2025) from favorable project mix; but share of JV profit -34.8% YoY to 168mn; admin expenses +44.6% YoY to 258mn from financing fees and IP Program provision (MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md Table IV).

Transfers: total 2,830mn (-20.5% YoY): consolidated group 977mn, JV 1,853mn (+87% YoY) from 21 JV projects; presales 4,511mn (condo 3,970 + BRI low-rise 541); backlog 34,681mn at 31 Mar 2026 (MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md Tables II, III).

Total IBD 31,197mn (D/E 1.41x, down from 1.49x); bond outstanding 12,117mn (18 LT tranches, BBB/TRIS); LT debentures 9,181mn (net); EBIT/finance cost ≈ 0.85x standalone; with JV income coverage ~1.74x (HC ORI.md Theme 6).
Cash 367mn — very low (HC ORI.md Theme 4); EBITDA-based interest coverage with JV income ~1.74x but without JV below 1x at consolidated level.
mdaSynthesis: Disposal gain of THB 96.24mn from Origin Kata Phuket (sold 50% to JV partner at THB 75mn MOU deposit received Feb 2026; BOD approved 27 Apr 2026 at THB 332mn) represents 5.7% of revenue and ~93% of normalized NP — this is non-recurring and inflates the headline materially (MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md Section I, VI).

Hotel segment operational: 9 hotels / 2,306 keys at THB 13,800mn asset value; Build–Operate–Exit–Reinvest asset-recycling model; Ibis Phuket Kata targeting Q2/2026 transfer generating liquidity for bond refinancing (MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md Section VI).

JV income deteriorated 34.8% YoY — of the 21 JV projects recognizing revenue in Q1/2026, condo-JV segment contributed 223mn but housing JV lost (23mn) and hotel JV lost (27mn); management targets The Origin Thonglor World Tower 4 in Q4/2026 as a flagship transfer (MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md Sections V, VIII).

Foreign customer backlog >6,500mn (Russia, Taiwan, Myanmar, China, Poland) — provides some USD/non-THB revenue exposure; regulatory risk from foreign customer transfers (customs, foreign exchange controls) not discussed in MD&A (MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md Section VIII).

FY2026 guidance: presales 25,000mn (Q1 pace = 18%), revenue 10,000mn (Q1 = 17%), CAPEX THB 680mn including Ecuador contribution — implies very back-loaded delivery in H2/2026 (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md Section 2026 Guidance; MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md Section VIII).
fsNotesSynthesis: BRI (Britania PCL, SET-listed) ownership percentage by ORI not confirmed in Q1/2026 interim sources — this is the gating question for ทจ. 46/2568: if ORI holds ≥90% of BRI, all intragroup transactions (loans, management fees) are exempt; if <90%, these are RPTs and intercompany loans (19,617mn separate-basis) would be Large RPTs requiring SH approval (ORI-RPT-2026-05-18.md Section 1).

Excess equity method deficit rose to 380mn (from 210mn at FY2025) — some JV entities have negative equity on ORI's books; specific JV names not disclosed; this may signal impairment or project-level losses requiring capital support (HC ORI.md Theme 5).

Deferred tax asset 1,209mn (large) — reflects tax loss carryforwards from JV losses; realizability requires confirmation of future taxable profits; if JV profitability remains depressed, DTA write-down risk exists (HC ORI.md Theme 5).

RealX digital asset (investment token) FVTPL: 294mn = 95% of all FVTPL financial assets; pricing and liquidity of this digital token are not transparent in the FS; at THB 294mn = 1.44% of NA — Medium RPT risk if token issuer is a related party (HC ORI.md Theme 5).

MOU advance 630mn for One Origin Hospitality/Ibis Phuket Kata: BOD approved THB 332mn acquisition of JV partner's share on 27 Apr 2026; if Origin Hotel PCL (listed sub) is the transacting entity, this may not be an ORI-level MT; if ORI consolidates it, size test required vs NA 20,471mn = 3.1% → Large MT (ORI-RPT-2026-05-18.md Section 3).

sixThemes.preCb: HIGH concern. EBIT/finance costs at consolidated level <1.0x if JV income is excluded; JV income is from equity-method JVs (not controlled subsidiaries) and is inherently variable. ORI's holding company structure means the parent has limited direct cash generation — it depends on dividends from listed subs (BRI, PRI, Origin Hotel) and JV distributions. D/E 1.41x vs RE developer norms ~1.0–2.0x; BBB/TRIS rating is lowest in the peer group (HC ORI.md Themes 1, 6).
sixThemes.salesQuality: MED. Backlog of 34,681mn (61% ready-to-move) and 25,000mn FY presales target suggest visibility — but Q1 pace tracks only 18% of annual target. JV revenue 1,853mn (Q1) from 21 projects is structurally lumpy. Non-recurring disposal gain (96mn) overstates Q1 quality. Foreign buyer backlog >6,500mn is a positive diversifier but introduces transfer risk (HC ORI.md Theme 2; MDA_ORI_2026Q1_T.md).
sixThemes.costMargin: GREEN for RE GPM (30.1% is a recovery). YELLOW for consolidated: admin +44.6% YoY from IP Program provisions and financing fees is a recurring cost that will persist; share of JV income volatile quarter-to-quarter. Net margin at 6.1% (normalized ~1.6%) is thin (HC ORI.md Theme 3).
sixThemes.workingCapital: MED. Cash 367mn is dangerously low for a company with 187mn quarterly finance costs; however, ORI is actively converting — Ibis Phuket Kata disposal proceeds expected Q2/2026; warehouse REIT injection planned (4 projects, 211,682 sqm). Inventory (dev cost 36,613mn) stable QoQ — not building further. OCF not directly extracted (HC ORI.md Theme 4).
sixThemes.cashFunding: HIGH. ORI267A (2,068mn) matures 10 Jul 2026 — 28 days from today; ORI269A (715mn) matures 31 Aug 2026; combined 2,783mn in <3 months against cash of 367mn requires timely bank drawdown and/or disposal proceeds. Refinancing plan: bank lines + Ibis Phuket Kata proceeds — Ibis deal timing is the binding constraint. IBD/EBITDA ~12–16x is elevated (HC ORI.md Theme 6; ORI-RPT-2026-05-18.md Bond Wall section).
sixThemes.outlook: Cautious. H2/2026 is heavily loaded: So Origin Siriraj (Q2), Origin Place Phetkasem (Q2), So Origin Bangtao Beach Phuket (Q3), The Origin Thonglor World Tower 4 (Q4). If these transfer as planned, FY2026 financials improve materially; but any slip in timing compounds the bond refinancing challenge. BRI RPT gating resolution is critical governance work.

PB.name: PRESIDENT BAKERY PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
PB.thesis: President Bakery is a high-quality, cash-generative domestic bakery franchise (Farmhouse) with fortress balance sheet metrics (D/E 0.09x, Current Ratio 8.41x, NPM 16.9%), but Q1/2026 net profit declined 13.4% YoY as cost of sales grew faster than revenue, and the multi-year ROE compression (from 13.2% FY2024 to 9.4% Q1/2026) reflects the limits of a domestic-market, price-sensitive consumer franchise facing raw material and depreciation headwinds.
PB.summary: President Bakery (PB) reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 1,721mn (+0.3% YoY from THB 1,716mn) and net profit of THB 296mn (−13.4% YoY), with GPM declining to 44.6% from 45.4% in Q1/2025. The cost of sales increase of +2.1% YoY (vs revenue +0.3%) was driven by higher depreciation (new investment) and input cost pressure — management cites lower main raw material prices (positive, partially offsetting) but the net effect is margin compression. OCF of THB 659mn against net profit of THB 296mn (OCF/NP 2.2x) is excellent and reflects the depreciation-heavy profile of a capital-intensive bakery operation. The balance sheet is a standout: D/E 0.09x, Current Ratio 8.41x, and virtually no IBD — PB is one of the strongest balance sheets in the FOOD coverage. Its major shareholder is Thai President Foods (listed), and it operates a joint venture President Green House Foods (Japanese restaurant). The RPT note discloses transactions with Thai President Foods and other related entities — trade receivable and payable balances — requiring size testing as the food-group interconnections expand under ทจ. 46/2568. Auditor (CPA No. 4753) issued a clean review conclusion.
PB.business: Producer and distributor of bakery products under the Farmhouse brand: (1) wholesale bakery (bread, cakes — primary revenue), (2) retail business, (3) fast food, and (4) export through domestic traders. Operates through a single reportable segment in Thailand. Subsidiary: President Green House Foods Co., Ltd. (Japanese restaurant, wholly-owned-equivalent), accounted as a joint venture at equity (balance THB 31.4mn). Major shareholder: Thai President Foods Public Company Limited.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 1,721mn (+0.3% YoY), cost of sales THB 941mn (+2.1% YoY), gross profit THB 756mn (−1.4% YoY), GPM 44.6% (vs 45.4% Q1/2025), net profit THB 296mn (−13.4% YoY), NPM 16.9% (MDA_PB_2026Q1_E.md).
