mdaSynthesis: Revenue essentially flat (+0.5%, 8.96mn): all growth came from volume (lower raw material prices partially allowed stability); management did not disclose pricing action (MDA_PB_2026Q1_E.md).
Cost of sales +2.1% YoY driven by depreciation on new investments — PB has been investing in capacity but this adds depreciation to cost of goods before revenue ramps (MDA_PB_2026Q1_E.md).

fsNotesSynthesis: RPT note: trade receivables and other current receivables from related parties disclosed, plus trade payables to related parties — Thai President Foods group is the primary related party as major shareholder; amounts not fully extracted from auto-ingest (NOTES_PB_2026Q1_E.md).

Joint venture President Green House Foods Co., Ltd.: Chiang Mai-registered, restaurant business, 50/50-equivalent ownership; carrying value THB 31.4mn (equity method, FY2025 audited THB 30.1mn) — stable, minor position (NOTES_PB_2026Q1_E.md segment evidence).

sixThemes.preCb: Green. D/E 0.09x, effectively net cash (Current Ratio 8.41x), no bond outstanding, no convertible note. PB is one of the lowest-leverage large FOOD companies on the exchange. Zero pre-CB risk.
sixThemes.salesQuality: Green. Revenue is clean — domestic Farmhouse brand sales, no non-recurring items, high brand recognition. Flat YoY (+0.3%) is a concern for growth investors but the quality of the revenue stream is high: recurring, stable, diversified channel (wholesale + retail + fast food + export).
sixThemes.costMargin: Yellow. GPM compressed to 44.6% from 45.4% — modest but directionally wrong. Depreciation on new capital investment is the proximate cause. Recovery requires either revenue ramp on the new capacity or input cost relief. Multi-year trend: FY2024 GPM 45.8% → FY2025 44.3% → Q1/2026 44.6% — partial stabilization.
sixThemes.workingCapital: Green. OCF/NP 2.2x is excellent; Current Ratio 8.41x. The business model generates cash ahead of accounting profit due to depreciation. No working capital stress visible.
sixThemes.cashFunding: Green. D/E 0.09x. The company is essentially self-funded through OCF. Capex is the only cash outflow variable — but given the strong current ratio, PB can fund substantial capital programs from internal resources.
sixThemes.outlook: Neutral. Revenue growth is essentially flat in a mature domestic market. The ROE compression (13.2% → 9.4%) reflects capital accumulation outpacing earnings growth. PB is a quality hold at the right price — but at PE 17.9x with flat earnings, the catalysts for re-rating are limited near-term.

PQS.name: PREMIER QUALITY STARCH PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
PQS.thesis: PQS is emerging from a severe tapioca starch downcycle — Q1/2026 marks the return to positive net profit (THB 19.8mn) after a THB 79.1mn FY2025 net loss — but the recovery is fragile (negative OCF of THB 155mn, current ratio 1.43x, three director resignations in April–May 2026), and the SET's high-severity inquiry into the Q1/2026 MD&A signals regulatory scrutiny at a critical inflection point.
PQS.summary: PQS reported Q1/2026 total revenue of THB 668mn (+39.7% YoY from THB 478mn), net profit of THB 19.8mn reversing the prior-year loss, and GPM recovering to 13.2% from a trough. The YoY revenue recovery is driven by cassava price improvement (THB 16.2/kg in March 2026 vs THB 13.4–14.1/kg at end-2025) and higher starch export prices, alongside the new Kalasin plant contributing volume. However, OCF was negative THB 155mn in Q1 — despite positive profitability — driven by working capital build (cassava inventory accumulation ahead of season-end). D/E has risen to 0.51x from 0.36x in FY2024, and Current Ratio of 1.43x leaves limited liquidity buffer. Three directors resigned in April–May 2026 (including a director and company secretary on 23 Apr, a director on 11 May, and replacements appointed 15 May) — an unusual governance event during a financial recovery period. The SET issued a high-severity inquiry on 22 May 2026 requiring additional MD&A clarification — the nature and outcome of this inquiry are not captured in vault but represent a regulatory risk flag. Loan to related parties at 2.95–3.60% p.a. and sales to related parties (THB 12.2mn in Q1/2026) require size testing. Auditor issued a clean review but with an emphasis-of-matter note on a retrospective inventory allowance restatement.
PQS.business: Mukdahan-headquartered tapioca starch processor: native and modified tapioca starch production (Mukdahan head office + new Kalasin branch opened Jan 2025), biogas electricity generation, solar rooftop power, and domestic land transportation/logistics (via Premier Logix Co., Ltd. JV with G&G 2015, established FY2025). Export-oriented: primary markets China, Japan, and premium markets targeted with low-carbon/traceable cassava output. Kalasin plant added >30% production capacity; modified starch facility in Mukdahan adds higher-margin product line. Major shareholders: Chanchungthaworn and Thawatchutikorn families.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: total revenue THB 668mn (+39.7% YoY), net profit THB 19.8mn (NPM 3.0%, vs net loss in Q1/2025), GPM 13.2%, D/E 0.51x, Current Ratio 1.43x, OCF −THB 155mn (MDA_PQS_2026Q1_E.md; dashboard).
Balance sheet at 31 Mar 2026: total assets THB 3,056.6mn, total liabilities THB 1,025.6mn, shareholders' equity THB 2,030.9mn, cash THB 288mn (MDA_PQS_2026Q1_E.md executive summary).

FY2025 comparatives: revenue THB 1,992mn (−27.1% YoY), net loss THB 79.1mn, IBD THB 698.9mn, OCF +THB 152.7mn — prior-year recovery demonstrates business can generate cash even in loss years if WC is managed (MDA_PQS_2025FY_E.md).
FY2024 comparatives: revenue THB 2,749mn, net profit THB 241mn (NPM 8.8%), ROE 11.4% — the reference 'good year' showing what the business can earn at favorable cassava prices (dashboard).
Interest-bearing debt at FY2025: THB 698.9mn; D/E 0.39x → Q1/2026 D/E 0.51x — leverage rising as the company funds working capital and new capacity (MDA_PQS_2025FY_E.md; dashboard).

PRG.name: PRANDA JEWELRY PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
PRG.thesis: PRG's Q1/2026 net profit technically recovered to THB 5.2mn (+183% YoY from a distressed THB 1.8mn base), but this masks a severe liquidity squeeze: OCF -THB 235.7mn, cash fell to THB 31.5mn (-50% QoQ), and ST borrowings surged to THB 371mn (+135% QoQ) — the inventory-financing cycle is stretching dangerously thin as rice revenue structurally declines (-24.1% YoY) and the export business is permanently closed; the FVOCI MBK position (THB 10,057mn) dominates the balance sheet but is locked up as a strategic holding and provides no near-term cash relief.
PRG.summary: PRG reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 548.5mn (-21.7% YoY) and NP THB 5.2mn (+183% from THB 1.8mn base). GPM improved to 11.57% (from 8.40% — raw material costs fell faster than selling prices). OCF was deeply negative at -THB 235.7mn: inventory build +THB 200mn (rice stockpile for domestic channel) + AP run-down +THB 38mn. Cash fell to THB 31.5mn from ~THB 63mn at end-Q4/2025. ST borrowings surged to THB 371mn from THB 158mn (+135% QoQ). D/E reported at 0.25x due to FVOCI MBK shares (THB 10,057mn = 28.12% of MBK equity) inflating equity base — true operating D/E (excl. FVOCI) is materially higher. CCC ~124 days. All 7 subsidiaries 99.99% owned — all intragroup transactions ≥90% exempt under ทจ.46/2568. Service fee to MBK parent: THB 12mn/Q — arm's length policy in place.
PRG.business: PRG (formerly Pranda Jewelry, now rebranded as food conglomerate under MBK 56.64% ownership) has three segments: (1) Rice — domestic milled rice under own brands (formerly exported, export ceased 56-1 Y68); (2) Food Center — restaurant/food court operations; (3) Solar — rooftop solar PV (+92.5% revenue, small base). Balance sheet dominated by FVOCI investment in MBK shares (THB 10,057mn = 28.12% of MBK) — this is a strategic circular cross-holding that distorts D/E optics. All 7 subsidiaries 99.99% owned.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 548.5mn (-21.7% YoY), NP THB 5.2mn (+183% from THB 1.8mn base Q1/25), GPM 11.57% (vs 8.40% Q1/25) (MDA_PRG_2026Q1_T.md).

OCF -THB 235.7mn: inventory build +THB 200mn (rice stockpile) + AP run-down +THB 38mn; cash THB 31.5mn (-50% QoQ); ST borrowings THB 371mn (+135% QoQ) (inspect.py hash 1d8aec64c8c1d865; MDA_PRG_2026Q1_T.md).

Balance sheet: D/E 0.25x reported (distorted by FVOCI MBK THB 10,057mn = 28.12% MBK); true operating leverage materially higher; CCC ~124 days (2-Analysis/AI-Generated/02-Health Check Log/2026_Q1/PRG.md).

FVOCI: MBK shares at market value THB 10,057mn (28.12% of MBK); FV changes through OCI, not P&L — no realized gain available without selling (2-Analysis/AI-Generated/02-Health Check Log/2026_Q1/PRG.md).

All 7 subsidiaries 99.99% owned → all intragroup transactions Exempt under ทจ.46/2568 ≥90% rule; largest intragroup loans: PRG→Ratchasima Rice THB 571.9mn (6.07% NTA), PRG→PRG Properties THB 309.7mn (3.29% NTA) — both exempt (2-Analysis/AI-Generated/06-Inbox/PRG-RPT-2026-05-17.md).
mdaSynthesis: Rice segment revenue -24.1% YoY — two concurrent drivers: (1) rice price deflation (domestic milled rice benchmark fell materially); (2) export business permanently ceased (disclosed in 56-1 Y68). The export cessation removes a revenue channel that cannot be simply restarted — structural, not cyclical.

GPM improvement to 11.57% from 8.40% YoY is genuine — paddy procurement costs fell faster than domestic rice selling prices in Q1/2026. However, absolute gross profit is only THB 63mn on THB 548mn revenue — insufficient to fund operating overhead at current scale.
Food center +0.6% YoY (stable) and Solar +92.5% (from small base) are both positive but individually too small to offset rice revenue decline. Solar remains a marginal contributor at current scale.

OCF -THB 235.7mn driven by inventory build (THB 200mn rice stockpile) — management is building inventory ahead of expected seasonal demand, but with cash at THB 31.5mn and ST borrowings at THB 371mn, the inventory financing is entirely debt-funded at what appears to be a high cost.

CCC ~124 days — unusually long, indicating slow inventory turnover in rice (natural for milled rice with aging/grading cycle) compounded by stretched payables. Improvement requires either faster domestic channel sell-through or higher rice price realization. (2-Analysis/AI-Generated/02-Health Check Log/2026_Q1/PRG.md)
fsNotesSynthesis: Service fee to MBK (parent): THB 12mn/Q = THB 48mn/yr. Rental from MBK: THB 1mn/Q. Sales to related parties: THB 2mn/Q. All amounts modest vs Large RPT threshold THB 282.8mn (3% of NTA THB 9,425mn). Classified as Medium RPT (Board approval level) — arm's length policy confirmed in place. (NOTES_PRG_2026Q1_T.md; PRG-RPT-2026-05-17.md)

All 7 subsidiaries confirmed at 99.99% ownership → all intragroup loans (Ratchasima Rice THB 571.9mn, PRG Properties THB 309.7mn) are ≥90% Exempt under ทจ.46/2568. This is a clean result — no Large RPT triggered by intragroup financing. (PRG-RPT-2026-05-17.md)

FVOCI investment in MBK: THB 10,057mn at Q1/2026 market value (28.12% of MBK outstanding shares). Changes in MBK share price flow through OCI — PRG's equity base fluctuates with MBK share price. If MBK price declines materially, PRG reported equity and D/E will deteriorate significantly.

ST borrowings THB 371mn: likely trade finance / short-term bank facilities for rice inventory financing. Interest cost at current market rates (~3.5–4.0% short-term) = annualized ~THB 13–15mn on the Q1 balance — not immaterial against NP of THB 5.2mn/Q. (2-Analysis/AI-Generated/02-Health Check Log/2026_Q1/PRG.md)

sixThemes.workingCapital: Red. OCF -THB 235.7mn in a single quarter on revenue of THB 548mn is a severe working capital drain. sixThemes.outlook: Watch-Negative. PRG needs rice price recovery, inventory clearance, and bank credit line rollover to avoid a liquidity event. The FVOCI MBK position provides balance sheet optical comfort but zero cash utility. MBK (parent, 56.64%) may need to provide intercompany support — which would itself constitute a RPT event. ROJNA.thesis: ROJNA's Q1/2026 reported net profit of THB 2,315mn (+636% vs Q1/68 loss) is 87% driven by unrealized FVTPL securities gains (THB 2,024mn) and JV share (THB 527mn); normalized operating profit is approximately THB 594mn (+18.8% YoY), which is solid — but SPP1 electricity contract expiry (Oct 2025) creates a permanent revenue step-down, the installment payable to a Related Party (739.8mn = 3.05% NTA) is a provisional Large RPT under ทจ.46/2568 before 1 July 2026, and the refinancing wall (THB 2,874mn due ≤12 months) is tight against cash of THB 2,858mn.
ROJNA.summary: ROJNA reported Q1/2026 total revenue THB 3,477mn (-9.0% YoY) and net profit THB 2,315mn (vs loss THB 427mn Q1/68). P&L decomposition: operating profit THB 359mn, share of ARAYA JV profit THB 527mn (residential land transfers), FVTPL gain THB 2,024mn (unrealized mark-to-market on THB 7,111mn securities portfolio). Normalized NP ~THB 594mn. Revenue breakdown: real estate THB 556mn (-12.3% — timing), utilities/services +28.3%, electricity -24.1% (SPP1 expired Oct 2025, structural step-down), EonMed medical segment THB 489mn (new, GPM 28%). Blended GPM 19.4%. The FVTPL portfolio (THB 7,111mn = 14.6% of assets) creates significant earnings volatility quarter to quarter. Key near-term risk: refinancing wall of ~THB 2,874mn (LT bank loans maturing ≤12mo THB 1,759mn + RP installment current THB 365mn + ROJNA277A bond THB 750mn) vs cash THB 2,858mn — essentially fully covered but zero buffer.
ROJNA.business: ROJNA develops and operates four industrial estates in Thailand (Ayutthaya, Rayong, Prachinburi) with primary tenants from Japanese automotive and electronics companies. Sumitomo Corp ~26% shareholder (RP). Business segments: (1) Industrial Real Estate — land plot transfers (lump, timing-dependent); (2) Utilities/Services — water, wastewater, electricity to tenants; (3) Electricity — SPP plant (SPP1 expired Oct 2025); (4) EonMed — medical (dialysis/hemodialysis, 78.19% acquired Jan–Mar 2026); (5) Investment portfolio — THB 7,111mn FVTPL securities. ARAYA residential JV provides significant share-of-profit contribution.

SC.name: SC ASSET CORPORATION PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
SC.thesis: SC delivered a solid revenue beat (+21.5% YoY) with OCF turning sharply positive (+108mn vs -1,697mn Q1/2025), but GPM compressed 606bps to 29.0% from condo product mix, LT loans to JVs (2,097mn = 8.39% NTA) are a Large RPT without confirmed framework approval ahead of ทจ. 46/2568, and 10,200mn in bonds mature within 12 months including 980mn due in the next two weeks at the time of writing.
SC.summary: SC Q1/2026 total revenue was THB 3,245mn (+21.5% YoY), net profit (attributable) THB 120mn (+7.2% YoY), NPM 3.7%. The revenue increase is driven almost entirely by condo segment (+156.7% YoY to 595mn) from point-in-time recognition as completed condos transfer — not a demand surge. Housing revenue grew a more organic +10.8% YoY to 2,215mn. GPM contracted 606bps YoY to 29.05% as condo margin (lower than premium SDH) diluted the mix. COGS grew 34.9% vs revenue 21.5% — a structural margin drag. OCF swung from -1,697mn to +108mn on 966mn inventory drawdown from condo transfers. SC raised 3,000mn new debentures in January 2026 as preemptive refinancing and holds 3,569mn cash plus 11,216mn undrawn committed facilities — liquidity appears adequate to manage the near-term bond maturities. The critical issue is LT loans to JVs: 2,097mn at consolidated level = 8.39% of NTA — a clear Large RPT under ทจ. 46/2568 that lacks confirmed board-approved framework, with the 1 Jul 2026 deadline approaching. Shinawatra family also directly holds SC debentures (537.80mn = 2.15% NTA = Medium RPT). Presales and backlog data not disclosed in public filings — a significant information gap.
SC.business: Residential developer (SDH premium brands: The Palazzo, The CREST, Grande Pleno; condo brands: I-Design, Scope); investment properties (office inc. Shinawatra Tower 3, retail, hotel — 545 keys across 3 hotels opening Q3-Q4/2025, warehouse 140,000/200,000 sqm); US real estate through SC ALPHA Inc. (4 LLC subsidiaries in Boston). All under Shinawatra family control. JVs with NNR1, SC Asset Three, SC L1, SCX H1, I-Store Sukhumvit, XW BP Two and others (13 named JV counterparties, SC holds 40–74.29% = joint control).
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue 3,245mn (+21.5% YoY), gross profit 943mn (-2.3% YoY), GPM 29.05% (Q1/2025: 36.11%), NP 120mn (+7.2% YoY), NPM 3.7%; EBIT 226mn, EBIT margin 6.98% (HC SC.md Themes 2–3).
OCF +108mn (Q1/2025: -1,697mn) — reversal driven by 966mn RE dev cost drawdown from condo completions; cash end Q1/2026: 3,569mn (HC SC.md Theme 4).
Total IBD 32,207mn; equity 24,981mn; IBD/E 1.29x; bond outstanding 19,900mn across 25 tranches (BBB+/TRIS); bond wall ≤12 months: 10,200mn (51% of bonds) (SC.md auto-thaibma-bonds; HC SC.md Theme 6).

Capital commitments for land: 4,135mn confirmed (up from 2,675mn FY2025) — active land acquisition continues despite market softening; RE dev cost total 41,277mn = 64.5% of total assets (HC SC.md Theme 5).
Undrawn committed facilities 11,216mn + cash 3,569mn provides adequate near-term liquidity buffer against the bond wall; interest coverage EBIT/finance cost = 2.11x (HC SC.md Theme 6).
mdaSynthesis: Condo revenue +156.7% YoY to 595mn is a point-in-time recognition event — completed condo projects transferring — not sustained organic growth; the forward condo revenue pipeline depends on the backlog which is not publicly disclosed (HC SC.md Theme 2).

Hotel segment: 545 keys across 3 hotels (opened Q3-Q4/2025), occupancy 69% Q1/2026 — still in ramp-up; hotel margin not separately disclosed but 69% occupancy suggests not yet break-even (HC SC.md Theme 2).
SC launched no new projects in Q1/2026 — deliberate pace moderation reflecting market caution; Q2/2026 launches expected but not specified in available materials (HC SC.md Theme 2).
Cost discipline: admin expenses -4.2% YoY; borrowing cost capitalization rate declined to 3.21% (from 3.81% FY2025) on new lower-rate debentures — a genuine positive (HC SC.md Theme 3).
US real estate (SC ALPHA Inc.): 4 LLC subsidiaries in Boston and Salem — 4 properties; no Q1/2026 fair value update disclosed; USD/THB FX gain 70.51mn went through OCI not P&L (HC SC.md Theme 5).
fsNotesSynthesis: LT loans to JVs: consolidated 2,097mn = 8.39% of NTA 24,981mn; Large RPT threshold = 3% = 749mn; 2,097mn exceeds threshold 2.8x; 13 JV counterparties identified (SC holds 40–74.29% = joint control, not ≥90%); board-approved framework status unconfirmed — must be verified in 56-1 Y68 or AGM 28 Apr 2026 minutes before 1 Jul 2026 (HC SC.md Theme 1; SC-RPT-2026-05-18.md Section 2a).
ST loans to JVs: 697mn = 2.79% NTA = Medium RPT; also requires board framework approval (SC-RPT-2026-05-18.md Section 2c).
Debentures held by Shinawatra family: 537.80mn = 2.15% NTA = Medium RPT; 37.5mn new SC Deb 1/2026 (2nd) issued to related persons in Q1/2026 (SC-RPT-2026-05-18.md Section 2b).

Loans to ≥99.99% owned subsidiaries (separate basis 9,507mn) — exempt under ≥90% intragroup exemption; Scope Company Limited (90.00% = exactly at threshold) requires ongoing % verification (HC SC.md Theme 1).

Shinawatra Tower 3 used as collateral for letters of guarantee (2,844mn) — not an RPT per se but creates structural linkage between family assets and SC debt obligations; no impairment indicators on investment properties in Q1/2026 (HC SC.md Theme 5).

sixThemes.preCb: MED. Shinawatra family controls SC and holds debentures directly — all family-issued debenture transactions are Medium RPTs under ทจ. 46/2568; LT loans to 13 JVs (40–74.29% held) = Large RPT unresolved. Family governance is concentrated but transparent. No CB signals; equity 24,981mn, A+/TRIS (error: BBB+/TRIS) rated (HC SC.md Theme 1).
sixThemes.salesQuality: MED. Revenue growth is real but quality is mixed: condo jump is one-time recognition from backlog (not new sales), and no new projects launched in Q1/2026. Presales and backlog data not available — a significant gap for evaluating forward visibility. Hotel ramp-up (69% occupancy) and warehouse (100% occupancy on operational units) are genuine positives. Rental revenue temporarily depressed by renovation (HC SC.md Theme 2).
sixThemes.costMargin: MED. GPM 29.05% is below the sector's typical 30–35% for SDH developers; the condo mix dilution (-606bps YoY) may be structural if SC is shifting its product mix. Admin leverage is positive (-4.2% YoY). JV loss (15.51mn) declining as JV condos near completion is a tailwind (HC SC.md Theme 3).
sixThemes.workingCapital: GREEN. OCF swing from -1,697mn to +108mn is material; RE dev cost drawdown 966mn confirms inventory is converting. Capital commitments (4,135mn land) show active reinvestment but also flag future working capital needs. Interest paid 404mn in Q1/2026 is significant for a company earning 226mn EBIT (HC SC.md Theme 4).
sixThemes.cashFunding: MED. Bond wall 10,200mn ≤12 months (51% of bonds) is large, but SC has 3,569mn cash + 11,216mn undrawn facilities = 14.8bn liquidity against 10.2bn obligation — coverage is adequate. Interest coverage 2.11x is manageable. BBB+/TRIS rating maintains market access. Near-term maturities (980mn by early June 2026) appear manageable given liquidity position (HC SC.md Theme 6).
sixThemes.outlook: Neutral-to-Watch. Revenue momentum exists and OCF is positive. The key unknowns are presales/backlog (not disclosed publicly) and whether the GPM compression is structural. RPT resolution is the regulatory priority. If JV loan framework is confirmed and backlog is healthy, tone could improve to Neutral.

SNP.name: S & P SYNDICATE PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
SNP.thesis: S&P Syndicate is a diversified food-and-restaurant operator in a structural revenue decline (FY2025 revenue −7.9% YoY, Q1/2026 revenue THB 1,305mn continuing the slide) but has stabilized profitability at a lower level through cost discipline, moderate leverage, and a high-gross-margin model (55.9%), with the overseas restaurant segment (Patara Fine Thai Cuisine in UK) and an impairment on one domestic subsidiary as the governance watch items.
SNP.summary: S&P Syndicate (SNP) reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 1,305mn and net profit of THB 43.7mn (NPM 3.4%), continuing the multi-year revenue contraction from FY2024 THB 6,201mn to FY2025 THB 5,709mn. The segment structure — domestic restaurants/bakery (82.4% of revenue), packaged food (13.3%), overseas restaurants (3.9%), others (1.3%) — shows domestic core under pressure while overseas (Patara Fine Thai Cuisine, UK) and packaged food provide modest diversification. GPM of 55.9% is high and stable (FY2025: 55.7%), which confirms the food model's cost structure is managed well; but SG&A absorption at the current lower revenue base is compressing NPM from 6.9% (FY2024) to 4.7% (FY2025) to 3.4% (Q1/2026 annualized). PwC (CPA No. 4298) issued a clean TSRE 2410 review. The FS notes disclose trade receivables from related parties (THB 19.7mn at Q1/2026) and an impairment allowance of THB 166.7mn on one subsidiary investment — the latter requires investigation as a potential value destruction signal.
SNP.business: Bangkok-headquartered restaurant and bakery operator: (1) domestic restaurants and bakery shops (S&P brand — main, plus Patara Fine Thai and others); (2) packaged food and bakery trading (manufacturing and distribution); (3) overseas restaurants (Patara Fine Thai Cuisine Ltd, UK, 50% JV); and (4) other supporting businesses. Operates across Thailand and has a UK restaurant JV. S&P International Foods Co., Ltd. is a 99.99%-owned subsidiary. The Chanchungthaworn family is the implied major shareholder group (per sector knowledge).
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 1,305mn, net profit THB 43.7mn (NPM 3.4%), GPM 55.9%, D/E 0.58x, Current Ratio 1.25x, OCF THB 277mn (MDA_SNP_2026Q1_E.md; dashboard).

Segment Q1/2026: domestic restaurants/bakery THB 1,075mn (82.4%), packaged food THB 174mn (13.3%), overseas THB 51mn (3.9%), others THB 17mn (1.3%) — pre-elimination totals; note prior period was larger at THB 1,378mn total (NOTES_SNP_2026Q1_E.md segment table).
Revenue trend: FY2024 THB 6,201mn → FY2025 THB 5,709mn (−7.9%) → Q1/2026 annualized ~THB 5,221mn — structural decline continuing but rate may be slowing (dashboard).

Net profit trend: FY2024 THB 427mn (NPM 6.9%) → FY2025 THB 271mn (NPM 4.7%) → Q1/2026 NP THB 44mn (NPM 3.4%) — profitability declining but OCF strong at THB 277mn (3.7x net profit) (dashboard; auto-ingest).

Impairment: FS notes disclose allowance for impairment loss of THB 166.7mn on one subsidiary and THB 1.4mn on another — the THB 166.7mn impairment is a material signal of value destruction in the subsidiary portfolio (NOTES_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).
mdaSynthesis: Industry outlook for 2026–2028: Thai restaurant sector expected to grow 2.9–3.9% CAGR to THB 350–390bn — SNP's revenue decline is below-industry, suggesting market share loss in addition to industry headwinds (MDA_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).

Raw material cost pressure persists: food raw material costs 'high and volatile due to weather conditions' — forcing some competitors to close, while SNP's scale allows it to bulk-purchase and reduce unit costs (MDA_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).

Consumer spending constrained: geopolitical tensions (Middle East oil prices, US economic slowdown impact) weakening Thai consumer purchasing power; incomplete long-haul tourism recovery adds to restaurant demand pressure (MDA_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).

Strategic focus: aggressive new brand launches in affordable pricing segment; strong brand recognition and chain network advantage vs independent restaurants; S&P positioned to benefit from competitor closures in the medium term (MDA_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).

Overseas Patara Fine Thai Cuisine (UK, 50% JV): carrying value THB 135.2mn at Q1/2026 vs THB 139.1mn at Dec 2025 — declining value; UK restaurant market is under significant pressure from post-Brexit cost structures; no impairment triggered yet but trajectory is negative (NOTES_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).
fsNotesSynthesis: Subsidiary impairment: allowance for impairment loss on investment in subsidiaries THB 166.7mn (stable from THB 154.6mn? — amounts at Dec 2025 vs Q1/2026 not perfectly delineated in auto-ingest); and THB 1.4mn on another subsidiary — material impairment on an unidentified subsidiary requires identification from the primary FS (NOTES_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).

Trade receivables from related parties: THB 19.7mn (Q1/2026) vs THB 15.2mn (Dec 2025) — modest but growing; ทจ. 46/2568 minimum threshold THB 20mn; at current trajectory may require formal framework before 1 Jul 2026 (NOTES_SNP_2026Q1_E.md accounting flags).
Accrued income from related parties: THB 5.2mn (Q1/2026) vs THB 4.8mn (Dec 2025) — confirmed at note level; stable, likely franchise or sub-lease income from related network (NOTES_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).

S&P International Foods (Thailand, 99.99% owned): equity value in parent financials THB 50mn — this is the entity that may be the impaired subsidiary given the THB 166.7mn impairment allowance exceeds THB 50mn book; the impaired entity is likely an overseas or domestic subsidiary not performing. Needs identification from primary FS (NOTES_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).

Patara Fine Thai Cuisine (UK, 50%): carrying value THB 135.2mn — no impairment allowance noted for this JV in Q1/2026; but UK restaurant economics are challenged. Auditor PwC issued clean review (AUDITOR_SNP_2026Q1_E.md).

sixThemes.preCb: Yellow. D/E 0.58x, Current Ratio 1.25x — the lowest liquidity ratio in IS1 FOOD restaurant coverage. No bond, but bank borrowings are meaningful at current leverage. OCF THB 277mn provides comfortable debt service cover. The concern is the combination of declining revenue, thin NPM, and the modest liquidity buffer.
sixThemes.salesQuality: Yellow-Red. Revenue is genuine domestic/overseas restaurant and food sales — no non-recurring items — but the structural decline (−7.9% FY2025, Q1/2026 annualized −6% from FY2025) is a share-loss problem in addition to market headwinds. The absolute GPM holding at 55.9% is positive and shows no revenue quality deterioration (price/mix stable).
sixThemes.costMargin: Yellow. GPM is well-managed at 55.9% (stable vs FY2025 55.7%) — cost discipline is intact at the gross profit line. The NPM compression (6.9% → 3.4%) reflects SG&A deleveraging as revenue falls over a largely fixed cost base. Recovery requires either revenue growth (SSS or new branches) or further SG&A restructuring.
sixThemes.workingCapital: Green. OCF THB 277mn (3.7x net profit), Current Ratio 1.25x — working capital dynamics are favorable for a cash-sales restaurant business. The low Current Ratio reflects the lease liability structure, not operational stress.
sixThemes.cashFunding: Yellow. D/E 0.58x is the highest in the IS1 FOOD restaurant peer group (vs M 0.43x, OKJ 0.41x). The subsidiary impairment THB 166.7mn has not required a cash write-off but signals a potential restructuring cost. No bond maturity wall.
sixThemes.outlook: Neutral. The industry is growing but SNP is underperforming sector growth — the company needs a strategic reset. The large-chain advantage (cost, brand, customer base) is intact; the question is execution of the affordable-segment expansion. Patara UK and the impaired subsidiary are drag items. Until revenue decline stabilizes and reverses, the multiple compression continues.

SPALI.name: SUPALAI PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
SPALI.thesis: SPALI has the best balance sheet in the residential peer group (D/E 0.81x, A/TRIS, interest coverage ~12x) and delivered the strongest presales momentum (+15% YoY), but GPM compressed to a multi-year low of 29.4% (down 535bps YoY) for the third consecutive year without a clear bottom in sight, a 13,500mn bond wall looms within 12 months, and the RPT exposure to the founding Tantipipatpong family cannot be confirmed because Q1/2026 FS Notes are image-based.
SPALI.summary: SPALI Q1/2026 revenue was THB 3,956mn (+6.9% YoY), net profit THB 402mn (+0.7% YoY), NPM 10.2%. The top-line recovery came on a low Q1/2025 base. Presales were a highlight at THB 7,694mn (+15.0% YoY), pushing the backlog to THB 16,049mn (+21.6% vs ~13,200mn estimated FY2025 year-end). However, GPM continued its multi-year decline to 29.4% (FY2024: 37.7%, FY2025: 34.3%), the lowest in at least four years. SG&A leverage is positive (down 13.8% YoY despite revenue growth), and finance costs fell 20% YoY reflecting lower-rate refinancing. D/E 0.81x is the best in the peer group and interest coverage (~12x) provides significant headroom. OCF was -563mn in Q1/2026 — negative but consistent with developer Q1 seasonality (working capital build before H2 peak transfers). The bond wall of THB 13,500mn ≤12 months (47% of outstanding) requires monitoring; SPALI268A (4,000mn) due Aug 2026 is the largest single tranche. SPALI's Australia operations target 10,500mn in FY2026 — geographic diversification that adds AUD/THB currency risk. RPT notes could not be extracted from image-based FS PDF, leaving the Tantipipatpong family transaction exposure unverified.
SPALI.business: Mass-to-mid-market residential developer operating across Bangkok and 36 provinces (detached, duplex, townhouse, condo) plus Supalai Australia Pty Ltd (Melbourne, Brisbane residential), office buildings (Bangkok CBD), and hospitality. Core brands: Supalai Vista (SDH), Supalai City Resort (condo), Supalai LOFT (condo mid-range), Supalai Premier (SDH premium). Founder Pratheep Tantipipatpong (34.53%) + spouse Achara (6.29%) = 40.82% family control.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue 3,956mn (+6.9% YoY), NP 402mn (+0.7% YoY), NPM 10.2%; presales 7,694mn (+15.0% YoY); backlog 16,049mn at 31 Mar 2026 (+21.6% vs estimated FY2025-end) (HC SPALI.md Themes 2–3).
GPM 29.4% (Q1/2025: 34.7%; FY2025: 34.3%; FY2024: 37.7%) — three consecutive years of compression, at multi-year low; SG&A -13.8% YoY, finance cost -20% YoY — both positive (HC SPALI.md Theme 3).

OCF -563mn in Q1/2026 (Q1/2025: OCF pattern not separately disclosed; FY2025 full-year +853mn) — Q1 negative is seasonal; DIO 1,751 days FY2025 (up from 1,369 FY2024, 1,244 FY2023) — inventory absorption slowing (HC SPALI.md Theme 4).

D/E 0.81x (best in peer group; peer range AP 0.87x, SC 1.29x, LH 1.67x, ORI 1.41x); bond outstanding 28,400mn (17 tranches, A/TRIS); bond wall ≤12 months: 13,500mn (47%) including SPALI268A 4,000mn (Aug 2026) as the largest single maturity (SPALI.md auto-thaibma-bonds; HC SPALI.md Theme 6).
Interest coverage ~12.3x (proxy FY2025 EBIT/annualized finance cost) — substantial headroom vs peers; IBD/EBITDA ~3.3x — conservative for the sector (HC SPALI.md Theme 6).
mdaSynthesis: Presales leadership: Supalai LOFT Q1/2026 achieved 50% take-up rate on a 3,000mn project — strong demand signal for mid-range condo format; provincial landed softened — geographic risk (HC SPALI.md Theme 2; SPALI-RPT-2026-05-17.md peer context).

GPM compression anatomy: three candidates — product mix (Supalai LOFT condo margin lower than established SDH), land cost inflation on Q1 vintage projects, and Australia margin dilution — root cause not confirmed from primary PDF (HC SPALI.md Theme 3).

Australia target of 10,500mn for FY2026 per IR materials — if mix tilts toward Australia (potentially lower GPM on AUD basis), domestic GPM may appear better than consolidated; currency risk also embedded (HC SPALI.md Theme 5; OI-7).

Treasury stock disposal (66.6mn shares, 3.41%) resolved by board 23 Apr 2026 — method and counterparty undisclosed; if sold to Tantipipatpong family vehicles, would be a Large RPT (SPALI-RPT-2026-05-17.md Section 3).
Finance cost -20% YoY — indicates successful rollover into lower-rate debentures; consistent with the A/TRIS rating advantage vs BBB+/TRIS (SC) and BBB/TRIS (ORI) peers (HC SPALI.md Theme 3).
fsNotesSynthesis: FS Notes Q1/2026 are image-based (scanned PDF) — text extraction was not possible in the JARVIS pass; RPT notes (Tantipipatpong family transactions) remain unverified; this is the single largest data quality limitation for SPALI (SPALI-RPT-2026-05-17.md summary).

Supalai Land Co. Ltd (100% owned) and Supalai Australia Pty Ltd (100% owned) are confirmed ≥90% subsidiaries — all intragroup transactions are RPT-exempt under ทจ. 46/2568; verification of full-chain ownership needed from 56-1 Y68 (SPALI-RPT-2026-05-17.md Section 1).

Land purchase RPT risk: if SPALI buys land from Tantipipatpong family-controlled entities, this would be a Large RPT (≥20mn = Large threshold for any RPT amount); historical precedent from other developers in the sector suggests family land sales are common — unverified for SPALI (SPALI-RPT-2026-05-17.md Section 4).

D/E trajectory: 0.81x (Q1/2026) = 0.81x (FY2025) = 0.77x (FY2024) = 0.67x (FY2023) — leverage creeping up 3 years consecutively, though absolute level still comfortable; DIO growth 1,244 → 1,369 → 1,751 days suggests inventory build is consuming capital (HC SPALI.md Theme 6).

Bond structure confirmed from ThaiBMA: 17 tranches, all A/TRIS unsecured; SPALI26527A (400mn) was the nearest-term maturity at 26 May 2026 — this has likely passed; SPALI268A (4,000mn, 5 Aug 2026) is the next large maturity (SPALI.md auto-thaibma-bonds).

sixThemes.preCb: MED. D/E 0.81x and A/TRIS are the strongest balance sheet indicators in the peer group. Founder family controls 40.82% — concentration is high but structure is straightforward (no pyramid or cross-shareholding complexity). RPT risk is unconfirmed due to image-based FS Notes — specifically, whether Tantipipatpong family sells land to SPALI is unknown.
sixThemes.salesQuality: LOW-MED. Presales +15% YoY (7,694mn) and backlog +21.6% (16,049mn) are the strongest forward indicators in the peer group. 50% take-up on Supalai LOFT is a demand quality signal. Provincial segment softening is a geographic risk. Revenue composition (98%+ property) is clean with no material one-time items.
sixThemes.costMargin: HIGH concern. GPM 29.4% is the lowest in 4+ years; three consecutive years of compression from 37.7% (FY2024) → 34.3% (FY2025) → 29.4% (Q1/2026) without a clear floor. Until root cause (mix, cost, Australia) is explained and a recovery plan articulated, this is the primary fundamental watch item.
sixThemes.workingCapital: MED. Q1 OCF -563mn is seasonally normal; DIO 1,751 days (3-year high) shows inventory build. FY2025 OCF +853mn suggests full-year cash generation is positive. Australia AUD-denominated inventory adds FX layer to the working capital picture.
sixThemes.cashFunding: MED. Bond wall 13,500mn ≤12 months including 4,000mn (SPALI268A, Aug 2026) is significant but the coverage ratio (~12x interest coverage) and A/TRIS access make refinancing manageable. Finance costs fell 20% YoY in Q1/2026 — actively managing refinancing cost. No covenants known to be breached.
sixThemes.outlook: MED. Presales momentum is the strongest signal in the sector. The business fundamentally works. The GPM compression story needs a resolution — either management explains the mix factor, or the compression reflects structural land cost inflation that will take 2–3 years to absorb. RPT note gap is the governance uncertainty.

SSF.name: SURAPON FOODS PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
SSF.thesis: SSF delivered a soft Q1/2026 with net profit down 34.3% YoY to THB 17.9mn (parent) as export markets — particularly UK/Japan — faced elevated energy costs and FX headwinds, while domestic volume growth (+23.3%) provided a partial offset; the balance sheet is conservative (D/E 0.54x, current ratio 1.50x) and dividend yield of 7.44% anchors income investors, but margin compression from 13.2% to 9.3% GPM needs recovery to justify a re-rating.
SSF.summary: Q1/2026 consolidated revenue was THB 1,311.8mn (MDA: THB 1,203.4mn from goods sales + service revenue), down 5.4% YoY on THB -69.2mn export decline. Net profit attributable to parent THB 17.9mn vs THB 33.1mn a year ago (-45.9%). Consolidated net profit THB 43.9mn. GPM compressed to 9.3% (from 13.2% FY/2024 and 11.8% FY/2025). The primary driver is the export sales decline — UK and Japan markets faced higher energy costs translating to reduced consumer purchasing power, and FX translation reduced per-unit baht revenue. The domestic response — growing domestic sales 23.3% YoY by expanding modern trade and distribution channels — is strategically sound but domestic margins are typically lower. OCF positive at THB 93.3mn. SSF paid a dividend for FY/2025 (yield 7.44% at THB 4.98), reflecting ongoing capital returns discipline. Two reportable segments: (1) Manufacturing/distribution of frozen seafood/food, (2) Cold storage and logistics. Related-party transactions appear at arm's-length commercial terms with other members of the Surapon group; a subsidiary has agreements with related companies covering purchases, sales, management, and technical assistance — amounts need confirmation for ทจ. 46/2568 size testing.
SSF.business: Manufactures and distributes frozen ready-to-cook and ready-to-eat seafood and other frozen foods for export and domestic markets. Key export markets: UK, Japan, EU, US. Standards: GMP, BRC, HACCP, ISO 22000. Two segments: (1) Frozen food manufacturing/distribution, (2) Cold storage/logistics. Part of the broader Surapon Foods group with intragroup supply chain agreements. FY/2025 revenue THB 5,723.4mn.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 1,311.8mn, net profit (consolidated) THB 43.9mn / (parent) THB 17.9mn (NPM 3.3%), GPM 9.3%, D/E 0.54x, current ratio 1.50x, OCF THB 93.3mn — all from reviewed FS (dashboard; MDA_SSF_2026Q1_E.md).

Export sales -THB 102.8mn (-9.1% YoY): UK/Japan primary markets affected by elevated energy costs and consumer spending squeeze; FX impact compressed baht-equivalent per-unit revenue (MDA_SSF_2026Q1_E.md).

Domestic sales +THB 33.6mn (+23.3% YoY): deliberate channel shift to modern trade and high-growth distribution channels to offset export slowdown — lower-margin domestic mix likely explains part of GPM compression (MDA_SSF_2026Q1_E.md).
GPM: 9.3% Q1/2026 vs 11.8% FY/2025 vs 13.2% FY/2024 — trend is deteriorating; the Q1 seasonal pattern and export mix shift both contribute but the decline is meaningful (dashboard).

FY/2025 full-year: revenue THB 5,723.4mn, NP THB 138.9mn — stable vs FY/2024 THB 138.8mn; OCF THB 529.2mn; dividend resolved for FY/2025 (yield 7.44% at THB 4.98 market price) (dashboard; 04-Coverage/FOOD/SSF.md).
mdaSynthesis: Net profit down 34.3% YoY (consolidated: THB 43.9mn vs THB 66.8mn Q1/2025; parent: THB 17.9mn vs THB 33.1mn). Export decline is the primary driver — UK and Japan weak demand on high energy costs; FX weakened the baht-equivalent selling price when converted from GBP/JPY (MDA_SSF_2026Q1_E.md).

GPM 9.1% on goods sales (MDA figure; 9.3% on total including service revenue per dashboard) — MDA notes this is lower than prior year without giving a quantified explanation of the GPM bridge (MDA_SSF_2026Q1_E.md).

Domestic pivot: company focused on high-growth distribution channels and modern trade as a deliberate offset to export weakness; 23.3% domestic growth is a material tactical success (MDA_SSF_2026Q1_E.md).

sixThemes.preCb: Green. D/E 0.54x, current ratio 1.50x, positive OCF THB 93.3mn, no going-concern language. Dividend paid for FY/2025. Financial position is solid relative to the sector.
sixThemes.salesQuality: Yellow. Consolidated revenue -5.4% YoY but domestic +23.3% partially offsets export -9.1%. The export decline reflects market-level demand weakness (UK/Japan consumer squeeze), not customer loss. However, the pivot to domestic lower-margin channels structurally shifts the GPM profile downward. RPT sales of THB 893.8mn require size testing.
sixThemes.costMargin: Yellow. GPM compressed from 13.2% FY/2024 to 11.8% FY/2025 to 9.3% Q1/2026. The drivers (export mix shift, FX, energy costs embedded in UK/Japan prices) are partly transitory, but the trend is concerning. If export markets recover and FX stabilizes, GPM should mean-revert; if domestic mix continues growing, the structural GPM ceiling may be lower.
sixThemes.workingCapital: Green. OCF THB 93.3mn positive; current ratio 1.50x. Working capital is healthy. Related-party receivables stable (THB 168mn) — no collection concern visible. The cold-storage segment provides fee income that smooths OCF.
sixThemes.cashFunding: Green. D/E 0.54x; no bond issuance noted. Company paid FY/2025 dividend confirming cash surplus. FY/2025 OCF THB 529.2mn strong. Capex commitments to third parties exist (note in FS) but amounts need confirmation.
sixThemes.outlook: Neutral-to-positive. Export market recovery in UK/Japan is the key catalyst — energy costs are easing, which should support consumer spending in H2/2026. Domestic growth momentum (+23.3%) provides a floor. The GPM overhang is the main risk — if export recovery is delayed, the Q2-Q3/2026 margin profile may stay compressed. AGM approved dividend, confirming management confidence in cash generation.

SST.name: SST PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
SST.thesis: SST is in acute financial distress: DSCR 0.23x, net loss Q1/69 (116.2mn), D/E 2.86x, and a MUD subsidiary loan of 200mn from a private individual lender that matured 5 Jun 2026 with no refinancing plan — compounded by three confirmed Large RPTs under ทจ.46/2568, goodwill 1,644mn with impairment indicators and no interim test, and a structural mismatch between core warehouse operations and FOOD sector classification.
SST.summary: SST reported Q1/69 revenue 626.8mn (−17.9% YoY), net loss (116.2mn), D/E 2.86x, CR 0.15x. F&B subsidiary MUD revenue fell −24.8% YoY; non-recurring items include PPE impairment 80.4mn and gain on sale Societe Langonnaise 36.5mn. Post-quarter: SST285A 450mn @ 7.10% issued 8 May 2026 to refinance SST268A — resolving the bond maturity but not the structural liquidity crisis. Critical item: MUD 200mn loan from private individual lender matured 5 Jun 2026 (19 days from report date at time of filing) with no refinancing plan disclosed. Three Large RPTs confirmed: director loan 60mn (5.1% NTA), MUD loan 150mn (12.8% NTA), SSTRT lease 345.7mn (29.4% NTA) — all requiring EGM + IFA before 1 Jul 2026. Goodwill 1,644mn has impairment indicators (F&B losses, revenue decline, branch closures) with no Q1 interim test. DSCR 0.23x over 5 quarters is the most severe deterioration in the IS1 coverage universe.
SST.business: Conglomerate with misaligned segment composition: core operations are warehouse/logistics (SST Warehouse 100%, SSTRT associate lease), but classified FOOD/Noodles via MUD subsidiary (F&B brand, 67% held). MUD operates retail food and beverage outlets (MUD brand). SSTCM (100%) is a cash management conduit borrowing at 8.25% externally and on-lending to SST. SSTRT (associate) owns warehouse properties leased back to SST — creating a structural RPT dependency.

TFG.name: THAI FOODS GROUP PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
TFG.segment: Agri-Food — Integrated Livestock (Poultry / Swine / Feed / Retail)
TFG.thesis: TFG's Q1/2026 NP of THB 2,047mn (+0.5% YoY) superficially stable masks a severe livestock price cycle downturn — Thai swine −31.3% YoY and Thai poultry −12.3% YoY — offset only by retail segment expansion (+30.7%, 690 branches) and Vietnam swine premium; the critical governance flag is TFG's guarantee of THB 23,301mn for subsidiary and associate debt = 104.2% of consolidated NTA (THB 22,354mn), which exceeds the ทจ.46/2568 Large RPT threshold by 35x and requires urgent verification of ≥90% exemption eligibility before 1 July 2026.
TFG.summary: TFG reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 17,877.9mn (+0.1% YoY) and NP of THB 2,047.1mn (+0.5% YoY) — flat on the surface, but the composition is dramatically different from prior year. Poultry revenue −19.5% YoY (average price 52.11 vs 59.44 baht/kg), Swine Thailand −27.1% YoY (average price 48.29 vs 70.33 baht/kg), Feed −1.6% YoY on volume growth. These declines were offset by Retail +30.7% (690 branches, +260 new stores YoY) and Vietnam Swine premium pricing (THB 77.50/kg vs Thai 48.29/kg). GPM improved modestly to 21.68% (+0.49pp). Capex surged to THB 1,321.4mn (+280.8% YoY) for farm and factory expansion. Interim dividend THB 0.085/share for June 2026. Bond maturity wall: TFG267A (THB 740mn) + TFG267B (THB 1,323mn) + TFG26NA (THB 1,000mn) = THB 3,063mn ≤12 months (45% of total bonds). Intragroup liquidity buffer: unused credit lines THB 17,316.6mn (consolidated). The CRITICAL IS1 flag: TFG guarantees THB 23,301.3mn of subsidiary/associate borrowings = 104.2% of consolidated NTA THB 22,354mn. Under ทจ.46/2568, any guarantee for an entity <90% owned is a Large RPT requiring shareholder approval. Verification of ≥90% ownership for each guaranteed entity is urgent before 1 Jul 2026.
TFG.business: TFG is an integrated agri-food conglomerate: (1) Poultry (broiler farming, processing, export) — largest segment; (2) Swine (domestic Thailand + Vietnam operations with distinct price premiums); (3) Feed (proprietary animal feed, primarily captive supply); (4) Retail — Thai Foods Butcher Shop, 690 branches in Q1/2026 (+260 branches YoY, targeting omnichannel fresh meat); (5) International operations in Vietnam (swine, premium pricing). Associate and subsidiary-heavy structure with extensive guarantees. Bond issuer; bonds listed Thai BEX. TU group relationship flagged for guarantee structure review.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 17,877.9mn (+0.1% YoY), NP THB 2,047.1mn (+0.5% YoY), NPM 11.6%, GPM 21.68% (+0.49pp), OCF THB 2,913.3mn, D/E 1.20x, current ratio 1.17x (inspect hash afa1361bdbd70dad; MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).

Livestock price environment: Thai swine 48.29 baht/kg (vs 70.33 prior year, −31.3%); Vietnam swine 77.50 baht/kg (vs 85.55, −9.4%); Thai poultry 52.11 baht/kg (vs 59.44, −12.3%) — cycle downturn clearly underway (MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).
Capex Q1/2026: THB 1,321.4mn (+280.8% YoY vs THB 347.1mn Q1/2025) — farm/factory expansion at peak livestock cycle trough (Health Check TFG.md; TFG-RPT-2026-05-17.md).

Bond maturity ≤12 months: TFG267A THB 740mn (14 Jul 2026) + TFG267B THB 1,323mn (19 Jul 2026) + TFG26NA THB 1,000mn (10 Nov 2026) = THB 3,063mn; unused credit lines THB 17,316.6mn provide buffer (TFG-RPT-2026-05-17.md).

CRITICAL: Guarantee for subsidiaries/associates THB 23,301.3mn = 104.2% of consolidated NTA THB 22,354mn; disputed AR THB 608.3mn (24% of gross AR, ECL 26.2%); farmer advance loans THB 440mn; ST loans to subsidiaries THB 7,589mn (NOTES_TFG_2026Q1_T.md; TFG-RPT-2026-05-17.md).
mdaSynthesis: Flat headline revenue (+0.1%) conceals a dramatic mix shift: Poultry (largest segment) −19.5% and Swine −27.1% as livestock prices collapsed; Retail +30.7% from 260 new store openings and Feed volume +4.3% (despite −1.6% revenue from mix) partially compensated (MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).

Vietnam swine premium is a structural advantage: THB 77.50/kg vs Thai domestic 48.29/kg — Vietnam operations command a 60% price premium, making the Vietnam swine business highly accretive to blended margins and providing partial offset to Thai swine cycle pressure (MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).

Retail segment strategy: targeting 690 branches by Q1/2026, up from 430 a year ago — management is betting the Thai consumer fresh-meat retail channel will provide a structural, price-cycle-agnostic earnings stream. If the store rollout maintains average productivity, retail will become the second-largest earnings contributor by FY2027 (MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TFG.md).

GPM +0.49pp to 21.68% despite severe livestock price declines — indicates feed cost savings (captive supply advantage) and retail margin accretion partially absorbed the price headwind. A modest positive signal in a tough environment (MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).

Capex +280.8% YoY at the livestock cycle trough: investing at the bottom of the price cycle is textbook agri-cycle strategy (buy capacity cheap, harvest at recovery). The risk is balance sheet leverage increasing during the earnings trough; D/E 1.20x is manageable but not pristine (MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TFG.md).
fsNotesSynthesis: CRITICAL — Guarantee THB 23,301.3mn = 104.2% NTA: TFG provides financial guarantees to external lenders for credit facilities extended to subsidiaries and associates totalling THB 23,301.3mn. At NTA THB 22,354mn, the 3% threshold is THB 670.6mn — the guarantee is 34.8x the Large RPT threshold. Under ทจ.46/2568: guarantees for ≥90% owned subsidiaries are exempt; guarantees for associates or subsidiaries with <90% ownership are Large RPT requiring shareholder approval before 1 Jul 2026. Breakdown of guaranteed entities by ownership % is the urgent open item (NOTES_TFG_2026Q1_T.md; TFG-RPT-2026-05-17.md).

ST loans to subsidiaries (separate FS): gross draws Q1/2026 = THB 9,257.5mn = 64.0% of separate NTA; ST loans from subsidiaries THB 7,526.7mn = 52.1% separate NTA. If any subsidiary is <90% owned, these are Large RPT on the separate FS basis — but typical intragroup cash pooling is expected to be ≥90% owned. Confirmation required (TFG-RPT-2026-05-17.md).

Disputed AR: THB 608.3mn (24% of gross AR, ECL coverage 26.2%) — a substantial uncollected receivable with contested status. If counterparty is a RP, this is both a credit quality and RPT flag. Breakdown not available in vault extract (NOTES_TFG_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TFG.md).

Farmer advance loans: THB 440mn outstanding — THB 440mn lent to contract farmers. ECL on non-current farmer loans at 60.6% suggests significant credit risk in the contract farming relationship. These are NOT RPT (farmers are third parties) but represent credit risk (NOTES_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).
LT loan to Thai Foods Feed Mills: THB 1,000mn due Nov 2026 — this intragroup loan has a specific maturity; ownership % of Thai Foods Feed Mills determines ≥90% exemption (NOTES_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).

KMP compensation +35.7% YoY — the most significant YoY increase in KMP pay seen in the IS1 FOOD coverage; in the context of flat NP (+0.5%), alignment between executive compensation growth and shareholder returns should be assessed (NOTES_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).

sixThemes.preCb: Yellow. D/E 1.20x (improving from prior year), current ratio 1.17x (thin). Bond wall THB 3,063mn ≤12 months, but unused credit lines THB 17,316.6mn provide a material buffer. No covenant breach identified but leverage trajectory requires monitoring with capex expansion ongoing (TFG-RPT-2026-05-17.md; inspect hash afa1361bdbd70dad).

Revenue quality is mixed: Retail +30.7% is operational but new-store rollout creates front-loaded cost with deferred productivity; livestock segments are price-cycle-driven. YTD share price +96.19% (inspect) suggests market already pricing in recovery — execution risk on that expectation is high (MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md; inspect hash afa1361bdbd70dad).
sixThemes.costMargin: Yellow. GPM +0.49pp despite severe price headwinds — feed cost advantage and retail accretion working. Capex at 280.8% growth adds depreciation from H2/2026 onward; margin expansion may plateau as new capacity depreciates. KMP compensation +35.7% YoY adds SGA pressure (MDA_TFG_2026Q1_T.md; NOTES_TFG_2026Q1_T.md).
sixThemes.workingCapital: Yellow-Red. Disputed AR THB 608.3mn (24% of gross, ECL 26.2%) is a significant credit quality concern. Farmer advance loans ECL 60.6% on non-current suggests systemic collection difficulty with contract farmers. Current ratio 1.17x is thin. OCF THB 2,913.3mn is strong, mitigating the near-term risk (NOTES_TFG_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TFG.md).
sixThemes.cashFunding: Yellow. Bond wall THB 3,063mn ≤12 months, partially offset by unused credit lines THB 17,316.6mn. Capex THB 1,321mn/quarter run-rate is a material cash drain. Guarantee THB 23,301mn is contingent but if multiple guaranteed entities draw under their facilities simultaneously, cash demand could materialise. Interim dividend THB 0.085/share is modest but adds to cash outflow (TFG-RPT-2026-05-17.md; inspect hash afa1361bdbd70dad).
sixThemes.outlook: Watch. The livestock cycle trough creates a temporary earnings plateau but TFG's counter-cyclical capex strategy, retail expansion, and Vietnam premium position it for recovery when Thai swine/poultry prices recover. The IS1 priority is the guarantee RPT review — if any associate guarantees require shareholder approval before 1 Jul 2026, the timeline is extremely tight. Share price +96.19% YTD prices in recovery; if the cycle does not turn or guarantee issues emerge, there is significant downside to current market pricing.

TFM.name: THAI UNION FEEDMILL PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
TFM.thesis: TFM delivered a strong operational Q1/2026 (+7.6% YoY sales, +11.9% NP, NPM 11.1%) with excellent balance sheet metrics (net D/E -0.27x, current ratio 3.2x), but the Board-approved USD 55mn majority investment in an Ecuador aquaculture business — TFM's largest-ever international capital allocation — needs screening as a Material Transaction under ทจ. 45/2568 before definitive agreements are signed, and rising fishmeal costs (31.2% YoY) are the structural margin risk.
TFM.summary: TFM Q1/2026 (three months ended 31 Mar 2026) reported consolidated sales of THB 1,325mn (+7.6% YoY), gross profit THB 265mn (-0.7% YoY), and net profit THB 148mn (+11.9% YoY) — the net profit improvement despite flat gross profit was driven by SG&A efficiency (-3.8% YoY, ratio 8.8% vs 9.8%) and a lower effective tax rate of 9.5% (BOI shrimp feed/fish feed tax privilege effective Aug 2025). Shrimp feed grew 13.1% YoY in sales and 16.0% in volume — the core engine. Fish feed was flat; livestock feed declined 17.4% on SKU rationalization and Pakistan exit. GPM declined 170bps to 20.0% on fishmeal prices +31.2% YoY to THB 47.18/kg. The balance sheet is very strong: cash THB 1,013mn, net cash position (net D/E -0.27x), current ratio 3.2x, interest coverage 11.6x. OCF was only -2mn in Q1/2026 — essentially breakeven (normal Q1 after strong Q4 creditor settlements). The Ecuador investment (USD 55mn, up to THB 1,711mn equivalent) approved 12 Feb 2026 is the dominant strategic and regulatory event: it constitutes TFM's largest-ever international capex, targets Ecuador's growing shrimp aquaculture industry, and construction period is ~2.5 years (completion ~2028). The Ecuador subsidiary had not yet been incorporated as at 31 Mar 2026 (FS Note 9). TU (parent, 51%) mentioned TFM's Ecuador investment in the TU Q1/2026 MD&A as extending the feed growth engine. TFM's MT/RPT obligations: the Ecuador acquisition must be size-tested under ทจ. 45/2568 once definitive agreements are executed.
TFM.business: Manufacturer and distributor of aquafeed and livestock feed in Thailand and SE Asia. Three product lines: shrimp feed (66% of Q1/2026 sales, manufactured at Samut Sakhon and Songkhla plants), fish feed (27% of sales, Samut Sakhon), livestock feed (5%). Geographic split: Thailand 90.4% + Indonesia 7.8% + Sri Lanka 1.0% + others 0.8% of Q1/2026 sales. Majority owned by Thai Union Group PCL (TU, 51%) — SET listed food conglomerate. Additional markets: Bangladesh (technology MOU Feb 2026). Ecuador strategy: invest in aquaculture business facility (construction start pending subsidiary incorporation).
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: consolidated sales 1,325mn (+7.6% YoY), gross profit 265mn (-0.7%), GPM 20.0% (Q1/2025: 21.7%), net profit attributable 148mn (+11.9% YoY); EPS THB 0.15 (Q1/2025: THB 0.13) (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md p.3).

Segment breakdown: shrimp feed 880mn (+13.1% YoY, GPM 21.9%); fish feed 356mn (flat, GPM 16.8% vs 22.5%); livestock feed 71mn (-17.4% YoY, GPM 14.7% improved); other 18mn (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md pp.4–5; NOTES_TFM_2026Q1_E.md Note 6).
Key ratios Q1/2026: ROE 28.1%, ROCE 26.3%, current ratio 3.2x, net D/E -0.27x, net debt/EBITDA 0.24x, interest coverage 11.6x — all strong and improved YoY (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md p.7).

Balance sheet: total assets 3,836mn, cash 1,013mn (vs 674mn FY2025), inventories 559mn, total liabilities 980mn (-13.3% QoQ), equity 2,856mn (+5.8% QoQ); no debentures — only bank loans in Indonesia (199mn ST + 34mn LT) (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md p.6).

OCF -2mn (Q1/2026) — Q1 seasonally weak on payable settlements after Q4 peak; FY2025 OCF +885mn; investing CF +342mn primarily from short-term investment liquidation; net cash +339mn QoQ (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md p.6).
mdaSynthesis: Shrimp feed volume grew 16.0% YoY on improved domestic demand across all Thai regions and market share gains; export softness (Sri Lanka flood impact, Indonesia competition) offset, but Thailand increasingly dominant at 90.4% of sales (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md pp.3–4).

Fish feed GPM declined 570bps YoY to 16.8% — more severe than shrimp feed; seabass competition from imports pressured the category; tilapia weakness from low prices; species diversification (gourami, catfish) is the mitigation strategy — not yet material (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md p.4).

BOI tax privilege effective Aug 2025 (shrimp feed Songkhla + fish feed Samut Sakhon plants): effective tax rate fell from 15.4% to 9.5% YoY; global minimum top-up tax 3.77mn is partially offsetting but net benefit is material (~THB 8mn/quarter vs base) (MDA_TFM_2026Q1_E.md p.3; NOTES_TFM_2026Q1_E.md Note 11).

The 72% pre-tax profit contribution from TASCO (a 23.07% road bitumen associate, Colas SA 24% shareholder) makes TIPCO's earnings fundamentally dependent on a business it does not control. fsNotesSynthesis: TASCO RPT analysis: equity income (THB 106mn/quarter) is NOT an RPT — it is an accounting recognition of share of profit, not a contractual transaction under ทจ.46/2568. Dividend income from TASCO (~THB 619mn/year historically) is also not an RPT (shareholder right). Only actual service/supply transactions with TASCO count (TIPCO-RPT-2026-05-18.md).

TASCO as Related Person: TASCO is likely an RP under ทจ.46/2568 through cross-board directors (นางอนุรัตน์ เทียมทัน is Chairman TIPCO + director TASCO; Colas SA directors sit on both boards). Actual transaction flows with TASCO are minimal: product sales to TASCO ~THB 0.28mn/year, services from TASCO ~THB 0.03mn/year, combined ~THB 1.5mn/year — well below THB 113.5mn Large RPT threshold (3% of NTA THB 3,784mn) (TIPCO-RPT-2026-05-18.md).

Colas SA as Related Person: 24% shareholder → RP under ทจ.46/2568. No large Colas SA transactions identified in available vault sources. Risk is future: if TIPCO enters into any construction/bitumen supply agreement with Colas affiliates, this would be a Large RPT (TIPCO-RPT-2026-05-18.md).

Siam Container Terminal (STC): STC is RP via Chairman นางอนุรัตน์ (holds 16.67% STC + director). Services from STC (shipping logistics for F&B): ~THB 19.48mn/year — approaching Medium/Large RPT boundary (~THB 20mn absolute threshold). Aggregation across 6 months may already cross THB 20mn → potential Large RPT (TIPCO-RPT-2026-05-18.md; NOTES_TIPCO_2026Q1_T.md).

Covenant uncertainty: 56-1 Y68 explicitly states management has uncertainty about covenant compliance in next 12 months. Specific covenant terms not disclosed in vault extract — IS1 must obtain bond/loan agreement covenants to assess breach probability. If breached, cross-default could accelerate all LT loans (THB 584.7mn) (NOTES_TIPCO_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TIPCO.md).

TASCO pledge: TIPCO has pledged its TASCO shares as collateral for loans. If loans are breached or called, the pledged TASCO shares (carrying value THB 3,161mn = 58% of total assets) could be seized — this would simultaneously eliminate TIPCO's principal income source and asset base (NOTES_TIPCO_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TIPCO.md).

sixThemes.preCb: Yellow-Red. Current ratio 0.86x (current liabilities > current assets). Covenant uncertainty explicitly acknowledged. TASCO shares pledged — collateral concentration. D/E 0.44x is manageable in isolation but combined with current ratio below 1.0 and covenant uncertainty, the near-term liquidity and compliance picture is concerning. Finance cost reduction is a positive trend (inspect hash dd0b029da8d4fdfa; NOTES_TIPCO_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TIPCO.md).
sixThemes.salesQuality: Yellow-Red. Core beverage operating profit is only THB 38mn — a minimal margin. 72% of pre-tax profit from TASCO equity income is passive and uncontrollable. Revenue −7% YoY in continuing operations. The earnings base is structurally fragile: one TASCO earnings shortfall quarter would make TIPCO nearly breakeven at the pre-tax level. Aura Active plant-based is a nascent growth driver (MDA_TIPCO_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TIPCO.md).
sixThemes.costMargin: Yellow. Core operating profit margin very thin (38mn on 498mn revenue = ~7.6%). Positive: finance cost −30% from debt reduction. Negative: normalised P/E ~70x on core operations only (if TASCO income excluded), indicating the beverage business alone is loss-making at a reasonable multiple (Health Check TIPCO.md).
sixThemes.workingCapital: Red. Current ratio 0.86x — current liabilities > current assets. Without TASCO dividend income, operating cashflow from beverages would be insufficient to cover current debt service. OCF THB 221mn provides a partial buffer (inspect hash dd0b029da8d4fdfa; Health Check TIPCO.md).
sixThemes.cashFunding: Yellow-Red. Covenant uncertainty is the primary risk — a breach could accelerate LT loans THB 584.7mn, which combined with current ratio <1.0 would create a liquidity crisis. Finance cost reduction is a positive indicator of debt pay-down progress. TASCO pledge means the key asset is encumbered (NOTES_TIPCO_2026Q1_T.md; Health Check TIPCO.md).
sixThemes.outlook: Watch-Cautious. TIPCO's core beverage business needs material improvement. TASCO income provides a profitable umbrella but is structurally uncontrollable. Covenant resolution, CEO transition (Sep 2026), and debt reduction are the three key FY2026 milestones. If any two go wrong simultaneously — covenant breach + new CEO uncertainty — market confidence could deteriorate sharply.

TU.name: THAI UNION GROUP PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
TU.thesis: Global seafood leader delivering its best topline since Q3 2022 (+7.6% YoY, ninth straight volume-growth quarter), but the quarter's headline profit leans on a one-off THB 361mn tax credit while leverage (Net Debt/EBITDA 5.09x), a THB 10.5bn 12-month debenture wall, and two open RPT/governance items keep the surveillance stance at Watch.
TU.summary: Q1 2026 was operationally strong: sales THB 32,054mn (+7.6% YoY, organic +9.3%), operating profit +29.0% YoY on lower Sonar transformation costs, and net profit THB 1,113mn (+9.2% YoY). Quality of that profit is weaker than the headline — stripping the one-off TTV deferred-tax benefit (THB +361mn net) leaves core profit near THB 752mn, a normalized NPM of ~2.3% vs the 3.5% reported. GPM of 18.2% sits below the 19.0-20.0% FY guidance band, with the US tariff reduced to 10% only for a 150-day window ending around July 2026 and skipjack tuna prices elevated. The balance sheet is the watch area: current debt jumped 17.9% YTD as THB 10.5bn of debentures (TU26NA/TU26NB/TU271A) enter the 12-month window against Net Debt/EBITDA of 5.09x — mitigated by an A+/TRIS rating and THB 28.4bn unused credit lines. Governance carries two open items: the THB 699.8mn S.M. Tower purchase from Chansiri Real Estate and the Fortress/Red Lobster USD 65mn unprovisioned contingency. KPMG review conclusion is clean.
TU.business: Manufacturer and exporter of ambient (canned tuna), frozen and chilled seafood, PetCare (via ~82%-owned i-Tail/ITC), and value-added products; US & Canada is the largest market at 43% of Q1 2026 sales, followed by Europe at 28%.
financialSnapshot: Q1 2026: sales THB 32,054mn (+7.6% YoY, -8.5% QoQ seasonal), net profit THB 1,113mn (+9.2% YoY), EPS THB 0.29 (+18.0% YoY) helped by cumulative ~19% share buybacks (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.2-3).
Margins: GPM 18.2% (-0.7pp YoY, below 19-20% FY guidance), SG&A/sales 14.5% at the top of guidance; EBIT +10.2% YoY on Sonar cost reduction (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.3, p.10).
Leverage: Net D/E 1.17x, Net Debt/EBITDA 5.09x, interest coverage 4.88x; current liabilities +17.9% YTD on debt reclassification into the 12-month window (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.8-9).
Cash: operating CF THB 577mn vs net profit THB 1,113mn (51.8% cash conversion); free cash flow negative ~THB 0.4-0.6bn in the seasonally light quarter (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.9; health check theme 3).
Market: THB 11.10, -13.3% YTD, PE 9.1x, PBV 0.93x, dividend yield 6.3% (dashboard ticker-summary).
mdaSynthesis: Growth is pricing-led and broad: organic +9.3% YoY with all four categories pricing up; PetCare standout at +22.6% YoY sales / +14.3% volume with premium mix at 51.5% of PetCare sales (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.5-6).

US Supreme Court ruling (22 Feb 2026) cut tariffs to a flat 10% for 150 days and opened a CBP refund path for IEEPA tariffs already paid — recovery amount and timing outside TU's control (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.2).

Brand outgrew private label (+12.5% vs +4.3% YoY), lifting brand share to 42.1% — consistent with the premiumization strategy management laid out at the 2025Q4 Opportunity Day (OPPDAY-TU-2026-03-09-2025Q4.md).

TFM committed up to USD 55mn for a majority stake in an Ecuador aquaculture/feed business (announced 12 Feb 2026) — extends the feed growth engine management flagged as a FY2026 driver (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.2).

Management held FY2026 guidance: sales +3-4%, GPM 19-20%, SG&A/sales 13.5-14.5%, CAPEX THB 5.5-6.0bn, payout >=50%; Q1 GPM sits 0.8-1.8pp below the band, so delivery depends on tariff clarity after the 150-day window and tuna prices normalizing (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.10).
Tuna (skipjack) at USD 1,693/ton (+7.6% QoQ) spiked in March; TU holds a 2-4 month inventory buffer against short-term cost pressure (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.5, p.10).
fsNotesSynthesis: One-off non-cash tax benefit: deferred tax asset THB 423mn recognized on TTV Ghana legacy funding confirmation, net THB +361mn after a THB 62mn FX loss — non-recurring, inflates reported NPM by ~1.2pp (MDA_TU_2026Q1_E.md p.2; NOTES_TU_2026Q1_E.md).
Receivables grew faster than sales: AR +11.8% YTD vs sales +7.6% YoY; overdue >3 months rose to 6.6% from 5.2% at FY2025 (NOTES_TU_2026Q1_E.md; health check theme 3).

Net derivative liability widened ~3.6x YTD to THB ~1,763mn as THB strengthened to 31.60/USD — directionally consistent with exporter hedging of USD receivables, not a speculative position (NOTES_TU_2026Q1_E.md Note 17-19; health check theme 4).

Debenture maturity profile: THB 13,297mn moved into current portion; ThaiBMA shows TU26NA (2.0bn) + TU26NB (4.5bn) due Nov 2026 and TU271A (4.0bn) due Jan 2027 (NOTES_TU_2026Q1_E.md Note 11; health check theme 4).
KPMG (Sujitra Masena, CPA 8645) issued a clean TSRE 2410 review conclusion dated 5 May 2026 — no qualification, no emphasis of matter (AUDITOR_TU_2026Q1_E.md).

sixThemes.preCb: No Pre-CB signal. Equity rose 3.1% YTD to THB 53.7bn, the KPMG review is clean, and interest coverage holds at 4.88x. Leverage is the stress point but A+/TRIS rating and THB 28.4bn unused lines keep this away from CB territory.
sixThemes.salesQuality: Good quality, no non-recurring items in revenue. Organic +9.3% with a ninth consecutive volume-growth quarter. Watch concentration: US & Canada now 43% of sales (4-year high) while Middle East collapsed -57.6% YoY and higher-margin Japan fell -8.4%.
sixThemes.costMargin: GPM 18.2% is below the 19-20% FY band — tariff costs hit Frozen (-1.1pp) and Value-added (-3.9pp) hardest while Ambient held at 19.3%. EBIT still +10.2% YoY because Sonar transformation costs dropped out of SG&A. Recovery to guidance needs the post-150-day tariff outcome and tuna price normalization.
sixThemes.workingCapital: Mixed. Inventory days improved 4 days YoY to 152 and inventory fell THB 1.1bn, but AR days rose to 40, overdue >3m worsened to 6.6%, and cash conversion was only 51.8% (OCF THB 577mn vs NP THB 1,113mn). CCC ~133 days is structural to tuna inventory economics, not new stress.
sixThemes.cashFunding: The red theme. Current portion of debt +THB 7.0bn YTD, THB 10.5bn debentures mature within 12 months (35% of total outstanding), Net Debt/EBITDA 5.09x vs ~4.0x comfort for an investment-grade FOOD name. Mitigants: A+/TRIS, THB 28,427mn + USD 261mn unused facilities, positive OCF. Refinancing plan is the priority RM ask.
sixThemes.outlook: Guidance held but back-loaded: Q1 sales run ahead (+7.6% vs +3-4% target on a low base) while GPM is below band. The 150-day 10% tariff window expires ~July 2026 — binary for H2 margins. Management expects pricing pass-through benefits to show from Q2 2026 (high season) per the Opportunity Day.

TWPC.thesis: TWPC's TW 2030 transformation is delivering measurable results: Q1/2026 revenue +5.2% YoY to THB 2,419mn with volume growth 12.6%, Starch segment volume +20.4%, Food segment contributing 45.2% of gross profit, GPM expanding to 21.2% from 15.0% FY/2024, and D/E at a conservative 0.53x — the transformation from commodity tapioca into high-value Food and Specialty Ingredients (HVA) is on track, though OCF is temporarily negative and a China subsidiary was established in April 2026.
TWPC.thesis_note: Tone is Positive with caveats: no HIGH surveillance flags; GPM expansion trend is multi-quarter; balance sheet conservative. OCF -110.3mn in Q1 is a watch item.
TWPC.summary: Thai Wah (TWPC) reported Q1/2026 consolidated revenue of THB 2,418.9mn (+5.2% YoY) driven by volume growth of 12.6% despite pricing pressure in the commodity starch market. The company's deliberate portfolio rebalancing under TW 2030 — shifting toward higher-margin Food and HVA (High-Value-Added specialty starch) — is showing in the numbers: Food Business now contributes 45.2% of total group gross profit (vs 23.6% revenue share in FY/2025), and Starch HVA is 47% of starch revenue (up from 45%). GPM expanded to 21.2% in Q1/2026 vs 15.0% in FY/2024 and 21.3% FY/2025. Net profit THB 121.2mn (NPM 5.7%), OCF temporarily negative at THB -110.3mn (seasonal working capital build typical for Q1). D/E a conservative 0.53x; current ratio 1.73x. FY/2025 turnaround net profit was THB 155.9mn vs net loss THB -71.4mn in FY/2024, validating the transformation. TWPC paid a FY/2025 dividend (DY 3.99% at THB 2.86). In April 2026, TWPC established a new subsidiary in China — a signal of regional expansion ambition. Segment data from Q1/2026 FS Notes confirms: Starch THB 1,727.9mn revenue (segment profit THB 94.6mn), Food THB 649.3mn (segment profit THB 152.4mn).
TWPC.business: Manufactures and distributes tapioca starch, specialty starch (HVA applications in food, pharma, textile), vermicelli, and ready-to-eat food products. Operations in Thailand and Vietnam (food business). Starch sold domestically and globally; Food brands include traditional vermicelli and RTE categories. FY/2025 revenue THB 9,295.9mn. New China subsidiary established April 2026.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 2,418.9mn (+5.2% YoY), net profit THB 121.2mn (NPM 5.7%), GPM 21.2%, D/E 0.53x, current ratio 1.73x, OCF THB -110.3mn — OCF seasonally negative on Q1 inventory build (dashboard; MDA_TWPC_2026Q1_E.md).

Segment Q1/2026: Starch revenue THB 1,727.9mn, segment profit THB 94.6mn (GPM ~5.5%); Food revenue THB 649.3mn, segment profit THB 152.4mn (GPM ~23.5%); Other THB 41.7mn profit THB 29.1mn — Food contributes 45.2% of group gross profit on 26.9% of revenue (NOTES_TWPC_2026Q1_E.md segment table).
Volume growth: Starch +20.4% YoY, HVA +5.8% YoY — volume leading revenue in a low-price starch market; Food volume growth via domestic modern trade + Vietnam expansion (MDA_TWPC_2026Q1_E.md).
GPM expansion: 21.2% Q1/2026 vs 21.3% FY/2025 vs 15.0% FY/2024 — sustained, not one-off; driven by HVA mix increase in Starch and Food segment expansion (dashboard; MDA_TWPC_2025FY_E.md).

mdaSynthesis: TW 2030 transformation agenda 'firmly taking hold' per management: Q1/2026 is positioned as the starting point of a new phase of sustained profitable growth. Revenue +5.2% YoY on volume +12.6% — the gap reflects ongoing starch commodity price softness (MDA_TWPC_2026Q1_E.md).

Packaging cost is the primary identified risk: resin, film, polymer costs rising; TWPC's multi-region sourcing has delivered cost offsets; no inbound logistics disruption to raw materials or outbound distribution disruption (MDA_TWPC_2026Q1_E.md risks section).

Food business: strong domestic momentum through modern trade and RTE segment; Vietnam food expansion continuing (+13% YoY export in FY/2025 per FY MDA); brand investments supporting consumer base growth (MDA_TWPC_2025FY_E.md).

HVA/Specialty Ingredients: volume +5.8% YoY Q1/2026; HVA now 47% of starch revenue; this segment has structurally higher margin than commodity starch and insulates TWPC from raw cassava price cycles (MDA_TWPC_2026Q1_E.md; MDA_TWPC_2025FY_E.md).

sixThemes.salesQuality: Green. Revenue +5.2% YoY driven by volume +12.6% in a soft starch pricing environment — volume quality is high. sixThemes.costMargin: Green. GPM 21.2% maintained at FY/2025 level (21.3%) despite pricing softness — confirms the transformation mix-shift is structural, not cyclical. sixThemes.outlook: Positive. TW 2030 roadmap is executing. Food segment mix continues growing as a share of gross profit. HVA starch provides structural margin floor. Vietnam expansion adds geographic diversification. The OCF seasonal dip in Q1 is a monitoring item, not a concern. WHA.thesis: WHA's Q1/69 revenue decline (−32.7% YoY) is primarily explained by land transfer timing in the domestic industrial estate segment, but three concurrent cash cycle signals (revenue decline, inventory build +29.3%, OCF −82.8mn) combined with a finance cost spike (+3.6x from a 3,500mn zero-coupon bond) and an unresolved Large RPT intragroup loan (4,027mn = 21.3% NTA) create a surveillance-grade watch until Q2 land delivery confirms recovery.
WHA.summary: WHA Q1/69: revenue 3,166mn (−32.7% YoY), NP 1,508.3mn, NPM 48.1%. Domestic RE revenue −51.9% YoY (land transfer timing — Thai-listed IE typically front-loads transfers Q4). Water +67.5% (WMS solid growth). Finance cost 309mn (+3.6x YoY) from new 3,500mn zero-coupon bond (effective rate 2.12%). OCF −82.8mn (cash cycle RED). Bond wall: WHA26OA 650mn (Oct 2026) + WHA26NA 2,500mn (Nov 2026) = 3,150mn ≤12 months. AR overdue >12M: 78.8mn (+258.7% QoQ, +3.6x), ECL covers only 12% incremental. One-customer concentration 495mn. Intragroup loan 4,027mn to WHAUP (71% — no exemption) and WHAID (99.99% — likely exempt): confirmed Large RPT at 21.3% NTA (7.1x threshold), WHAUP vs WHAID breakdown unknown. Rate asymmetry: WHA lends at 1.40-3.29%, borrows back at 0.55% — cost of debt (zero-coupon bond 2.12%) exceeds rate on reverse loan.
WHA.business: Integrated industrial estate and infrastructure conglomerate.
