XBIO.name: X BIOSCIENCE PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED
XBIO.thesis: XBIO is a micro-cap shell-like entity with 8 consecutive quarters of net loss totalling over THB 730mn, a going-concern emphasis-of-matter from its Q1/2026 reviewer, current ratio below 1.0x (0.97x), serial capital raises and warrant issuances (W8, W9 pending), a completed tender offer that restructured its shareholder base, and a BOD announcement in June 2026 of another capital increase plus XBIO-W9 — the company appears to be a serial diluter undergoing operational transformation from food into construction services, with no clear path to sustainable earnings.
XBIO.summary: XBIO reported Q1/2026 revenue of THB 85.3mn (+55.7% YoY) with a net loss of THB -335.9mn (NPM -394.6%). The revenue growth is attributable to the construction services business — a new segment the company entered following its strategic pivot. However, the GPM is 34.2% while the NPM is -394.6%, implying massive below-the-line losses that dwarf the gross profit. The FS Notes reveal a going-concern note (Note 2) describing 'continuous operating losses' and uncertainty about working capital for future project development. The Q1/2026 reviewer (A&A Office) issued an emphasis-of-matter paragraph drawing attention to this uncertainty. Since late 2025, XBIO has undergone: a capital reduction and increase (March 2026), a completed tender offer (result reported May 2026), multiple director resignations (CFO resigned April 2026, replaced by Acting CFO; COO Food Division resigned May 2026), and a June 2026 BOD resolution for another capital increase plus XBIO-W9 issuance. From a surveillance standpoint, XBIO is a complex governance situation with high dilution risk, regulatory attention (multiple SET clarification requests), and construction-contract revenue recognition complexity.
XBIO.business: Originally classified as FOOD sector but operationally transitioning. Current activities: (1) Food business — original FOOD sector activities (revenue declining sharply); (2) Construction services — new segment; contracts recognise revenue over time on input method (% completion); also acquired Chokdee Dimsum Corporation Co., Ltd. (Feb 2026, classified asset acquisition). Warrant overhang: XBIO-W8 being exercised (result filed Jun 2026); XBIO-W9 issuance approved Jun 2026 BOD. Market cap THB ~1.0bn at THB 0.08/share.
financialSnapshot: Q1/2026: revenue THB 85.3mn (+55.7% YoY vs THB 53.3mn Q1/2025), net loss THB -335.9mn (NPM -394.6%), GPM 34.2% (gross profit THB 28.4mn), D/E 1.11x, current ratio 0.97x, OCF THB -42.7mn — massive below-gross-profit losses (dashboard; MDA_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

FY/2025: revenue THB 135.9mn, net loss THB -468.9mn (NPM -358.2%), OCF THB -75.3mn, D/E 1.73x — deteriorated from FY/2024 net loss THB -260.2mn; 8 consecutive loss quarters (dashboard; XBIO-bundle-2026-05-04.md).

Going-concern note: auditor Q1/2026 reviewer drew attention (emphasis of matter, not qualification) to the company's continuous operating losses and 'uncertainty of significant effect on operations' — company prepared FS on going-concern basis assuming future working capital from project development (AUDITOR_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md; NOTES_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md Note 2).

Construction contract revenue Q1/2026: THB 83.0mn out of total THB 85.3mn — the food business is essentially residual; construction revenue recognises over time (input method); major accounting estimates involve contract cost estimation, ECL on contract assets, and liquidated-damages risk (NOTES_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md; MDA_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

Below-gross-profit losses: gross profit THB 28.4mn vs net loss THB -335.9mn — implies non-cash/non-recurring or overhead charges of ~THB 364mn in Q1/2026; specific nature (impairment, provisions, FX, write-offs) not fully extracted from this vault version; needs primary FS P&L review.
mdaSynthesis: Revenue increased +55.7% YoY (THB 83.0mn from construction, vs THB 53.3mn Q1/2025) — primarily from the construction services business described as the new core strategy (MDA_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

Cost of sales: THB 54.6mn (+51.3% YoY) — GPM 34.2% suggesting healthy unit-level project margins; however the gap between gross profit (THB 28.4mn) and net loss (THB -335.9mn) implies ~THB 364mn in operating/other expenses that are not explained in the MDA extract (MDA_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

Finance costs decreased THB 1.0mn (-16.9%) — 'mainly due to additional borrowings used for business operations' (MDA text appears internally inconsistent — decreasing finance costs from additional borrowings; may be a translation artifact) (MDA_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

Cash flow: the company reported an increase in cash of THB 25.9mn in Q1/2026 — positive vs OCF -42.7mn, implying financing inflows (likely from warrant exercises or new borrowings) of ~THB 68.6mn in Q1 (MDA_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md; dashboard).

Construction contract recognition: revenue recognised over time using input method; management estimates contract costs and assesses liquidated-damages probability before recognising revenue — significant estimation risk on complex projects (NOTES_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md accounting policies).
fsNotesSynthesis: Going-concern Note 2: the company explicitly discloses continuous operating losses and states FS are prepared on going-concern basis assuming future working capital from project development — the auditor's emphasis of matter amplifies this. This is a material disclosure not buried in the notes (NOTES_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md Note 2; AUDITOR_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

Construction contract accounting: costs recognise as incurred; revenue recognises as performance obligation satisfied (input method); contract assets arise when cumulative revenue > billings; contract liabilities when billings > revenue. Provision for anticipated losses on projects is booked in full when loss is 'ascertained' — any project turning loss-making triggers immediate full provision (NOTES_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

Accounting policy change: construction services business adopted new recognition policy in Q1/2026 — this is a material policy change that makes prior periods not directly comparable for the construction segment (NOTES_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

Revenue concentration: THB 83.0mn from construction in Q1/2026 — counterparty concentration and project pipeline not disclosed in this vault version; construction revenue is inherently lumpy and project-completion dependent.

Equity structure: serial warrant and capital raise cycle: W8 exercise results filed Jun 2026; W9 issuance approved BOD Jun 2026 alongside another capital increase — each exercise creates dilution and cash inflow but also signals the company cannot fund itself from operations (04-Coverage/FOOD/XBIO.md; NOTES_XBIO_2026Q1_E.md).

sixThemes.preCb: Red. Going-concern emphasis of matter. 8 consecutive loss quarters. Current ratio 0.97x (below 1.0). The BOD June 2026 approved a capital increase to provide working capital — a signal that the company views its liquidity as inadequate from operations. XBIO-W9 at what exercise price needs to be confirmed before dilution math can be assessed.
sixThemes.salesQuality: Yellow. Construction revenue +55.7% YoY but Q1/2025 base was tiny (THB 53.3mn). Input-method recognition makes revenue dependent on management's cost estimates — if projects overrun, revenue gets reversed. No disclosure of contract backlog, number of active projects, or customer identity in this vault version. Food business revenue is residual.
sixThemes.costMargin: Red. Gross profit THB 28.4mn but net loss THB -335.9mn — the ~THB 364mn gap is unaccounted for in the MDA extract. This pattern is consistent with impairments, loss provisions, or restructuring charges buried below the gross line. Without the full P&L breakdown, the true economic loss is unclear. Cumulative losses FY/2025 net loss THB -468.9mn; Q1/2026 THB -335.9mn — burning THB 100mn+ per quarter even in what appears to be a revenue-growth period.
sixThemes.workingCapital: Red. Current ratio 0.97x, OCF -42.7mn, and financing inflows required to maintain cash. Contract assets (construction-in-progress billings) could be large relative to the balance sheet — ECL on these is a key judgement item. Collection risk from construction clients.
sixThemes.cashFunding: Red. Serial capital raises (W8 ongoing, W9 approved Jun 2026) and BOD-approved capital increase — the company is dependent on equity market access to fund operations. D/E 1.11x. If equity markets close or share price falls further (already at THB 0.08), the funding model breaks. The tender offer completed in May 2026 changed the shareholder base, but the new majority shareholder's support for further capital raises is unknown.
sixThemes.outlook: Watch. Construction services is a legitimate pivot if the company can win and execute large enough projects to cover its overhead. The June 2026 BOD resolution (capital increase + W9 + director changes + CFO appointment + head office location change) signals the company is in active restructuring. The going-concern note and auditor emphasis of matter are the most material signals that this is a high-risk surveillance case.

SSSG direction in Q1/2026 not confirmed from primary source (aggregator proxy only). Lease liabilities THB 742mn = 69% of total IBD (THB 1,071mn); D/E 1.10x — debt is predominantly TFRS 16 lease, not financial debt. D/E optics overstate financial leverage; lease-adjusted EBITDA is the correct coverage metric. ZEN–CPN lease RPT: if AGB Siblings (25% of ZEN) are members of the Chirathivat family (which also controls ~30% of CPN), then CPN = RP of ZEN and all ZEN–CPN mall leases = RPT. Large RPT threshold THB 43.9mn (3% of NTA THB 1,464mn) — any annual CPN lease above this requires board/shareholder approval and IFA opinion. This is unresolved before 1 July 2026.
ZEN.business: ZEN Corp operates restaurant chains in Thailand (and selected international markets) under 13 brands including ZEN Japanese, AKA Japanese, Tsubohachi, On the Table, and Thai brands. Business model: leased restaurant premises (majority in CPN-managed malls — CPN = Central Pattana, Chirathivat family), franchise fees, and food production kitchen supply. Chirathivat direct: ~24.87%; AGB Siblings: ~25% (ownership unknown — possible Chirathivat). TFRS 16 lease liabilities drive D/E. NP trend: THB 158mn (FY66) → THB 57mn (FY67) → THB 46mn (FY68) — structural decline reversed by Q1/2026 NP uptick.

mdaSynthesis: Revenue -1.5% YoY on aggregator basis — slight volume decline partially offset by price increases and product mix. SSSG directional data not available from aggregator proxy; primary MD&A PDF returned HTTP 403 throughout the research period. This is a material data quality limitation.

Branch rationalization: 17 closures in FY68 improved unit economics by removing underperforming locations. Net branch count ~165; the rationalization effect should have stabilized the cost base going into FY2026. Q1/2026 NP uptick (+23% YoY) may be partly attributable to this cleanup.
International: Laos KoLao partnership operational — contribution size not quantified in aggregator data; Philippines in development stage. International represents a small but growing optionality.

13 brands (8 Japanese, 5 Thai): Japanese brands benefit from sustained consumer preference for Japanese dining in Thailand; Thai brands provide portfolio breadth but require different operational economics. Brand portfolio strategy review pending management clarification.

fsNotesSynthesis: ZEN–CPN lease RPT analysis: Chirathivat family holds ~24.87% direct in ZEN; AGB Siblings holds ~25% of ZEN (ownership identity unknown). If AGB = Chirathivat → Chirathivat aggregate >10% in ZEN AND Chirathivat controls CPN (CPN is Central Pattana, majority Chirathivat-owned) → CPN = RP of ZEN → all ZEN–CPN mall leases = RPT under ทจ.46/2568. Large RPT threshold THB 43.9mn/year (3% NTA). ZEN's annual CPN lease cost likely materially exceeds this threshold given ~165 branches in CPN malls. This is HIGH severity — unresolved before 1 Jul 2026. (2-Analysis/AI-Generated/06-Inbox/ZEN-RPT-2026-05-18.md; 2-Analysis/AI-Generated/02-Health Check Log/2026_Q1/ZEN.md)

Franchise/management fees between ZEN holding company and its 100% subsidiaries = Exempt under ทจ.46/2568 (≥90% intragroup). This is a clean result for the intragroup fee structure. (2-Analysis/AI-Generated/06-Inbox/ZEN-RPT-2026-05-18.md)

Lease liabilities THB 742mn (TFRS 16): right-of-use assets on the balance sheet with corresponding lease liabilities; EBITDA inflated by IFRS 16 add-back (depreciation of ROU asset + lease interest); true free cash flow requires deducting lease principal payments. OCF FY68 THB 538mn includes TFRS 16 lease payments as operating/financing — interpretation matters for true cash generation.

CCC deterioration from 4.3 to 43.1 days (FY67 to FY68): significant receivables extension or payables compression — in a restaurant business, this usually reflects delayed collection from corporate/catering accounts or faster supplier payments. Requires primary FS Notes for full diagnosis.

sixThemes.preCb: Yellow. Reported D/E 1.10x is predominantly TFRS 16 lease liabilities (THB 742mn of THB 1,071mn IBD = 69%). Financial D/E ex-leases estimated ~0.34x — not concerning. However, TFRS 16 lease obligations are contractual and must be serviced. NTA THB 1,464mn is modest; OCF THB 538mn (FY68) provides reasonable TFRS 16 lease service coverage (~1.4x). No bond outstanding. The audit emphasis of matter overhang is the key balance sheet risk signal.
sixThemes.salesQuality: Yellow. Revenue -1.5% YoY in an environment where branch count fell 9% (17 closures) — this implies surviving branches grew revenue, which is a marginally positive SSSG signal, but unconfirmed without primary source. NPM of 1.6% leaves virtually no margin for error. Thin profitability at a PE multiple of ~32.7x (health check) implies significant upside-pricing of a recovery that remains unconfirmed.
sixThemes.costMargin: Yellow. Branch closure program should have improved unit economics. TFRS 16 depreciation and interest charges inflate below-EBITDA costs. True restaurant-level contribution margin (before central overhead and TFRS 16) is the key metric — not available from aggregator proxy. If same-store labor and food costs are rising (Thai minimum wage increase Jan 2026), margin improvement will be harder to sustain.
sixThemes.workingCapital: Yellow. CCC deteriorated from 4.3 to 43.1 days FY67→FY68 — significant working capital elongation. Q1/2026 OCF THB 57.8mn vs NP THB 15.7mn = 3.7x OCF/NP ratio (good), but the FY68 CCC trend is concerning. Primary FS notes needed to diagnose receivables vs payables.
sixThemes.cashFunding: Green-Yellow. OCF FY68 THB 538mn covers lease obligations and operating needs. No bond wall. Financial IBD (ex-TFRS 16) is modest. The key risk is if lease renewals (particularly in CPN malls) come at significantly higher rates — ZEN has limited bargaining power given its mall dependency on Chirathivat-controlled properties.
sixThemes.outlook: Cautiously-Watch. Q1/2026 NP uptick is a positive signal but at 1.6% NPM and PE 32.7x, the market has priced in a recovery that requires sustained SSSG improvement, margin expansion, and resolution of the audit emphasis of matter. The ทจ.46/2568 ZEN–CPN lease RPT risk is the most actionable near-term item — if CPN lease costs are classified as Large RPT, ZEN may need shareholder approval for renewals, adding governance complexity. Data quality limitation (PDF inaccessible) prevents full conviction.
